**Extract:**

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business.

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

Consider the following **three** sources of finance Tokumbo could use for the new vehicles:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

Which source should he choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
Leasing allows SA to use the safari vehicles without requiring a large upfront payment because costs are spread over time. This helps manage cash flow **[An]**, which is an important consideration for a small business like SA **[Ap]. **Additionally, leasing makes it easier to upgrade vehicles regularly, ensuring SA always has modern, reliable transport for safari tours **[An]**

A bank loan could provide the necessary funds, but it would require repayment with interest, adding to SA's costs **[An]**. Given that interest rates are 2% **[Ap]**, this might seem attractive. However, as a sole trader, Tokumbo would be personally liable for the loan, putting his assets at risk if SA struggled to make repayments **[An]**

Retained profit, if available, would be the cheapest option. However, SA has only been operating for 2 years **[Ap]**, so it is unlikely to have accumulated enough retained profit to purchase the vehicles outright **[An]**. Additionally, using all available retained profit could leave SA without reserves for emergencies  **[An]**

Leasing offers the most flexible and low-risk option **[E]** for SA to acquire new vehicles, supporting its growth plans without overstretching its financial resources **[E]**. Although SA will never own the vehicles, it will be able to use them to provide safari tours, and there is less personal risk for sole trader Tokumbo **[Ap]** if the business fails **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think cash flow forecasts always aid managers' decision-making? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
On the positive side, cash flow forecasts provide managers with advance warning of potential cash shortages **[K]** enabling them to arrange overdrafts or loans before problems occur, which helps prevent business failure **[An]**

Cash flow forecasts also help managers plan timing of major purchases and investments **[K]** allowing them to schedule expenditure when cash is available and avoid financial difficulties **[An]**

However, cash flow forecasts are based on estimates and predictions which may prove inaccurate **[K]** leading managers to make poor decisions based on unreliable information **[An]**

Overall, whether cash flow forecasts aid decision-making depends on their accuracy and how managers use them. Well-researched forecasts with realistic assumptions are more likely to improve decision-making **[E]** while inaccurate forecasts based on poor data may actually mislead managers and result in wrong decisions

Given these mixed outcomes, businesses should focus on using reliable data sources, regular updates, and conservative estimates when preparing cash flow forecasts. This approach helps ensure that forecasts genuinely support rather than hinder effective management decisions **[E]**

>     - Sales growth needed to sustain 20 % increase may not materialise
>     - If outflows remain high, stronger inflows alone might not prevent liquidity shortages
> - **15% decrease in monthly cash outflows**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Cutting outflows by 15 % lowers monthly cash drain → net cash improves across all months
>     - October–December outflows of \$1 950–2 050 k fall by about \$292–308 k → negative months turn closer to break-even or positive
>     - Reduces need for external finance and interest costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - May require cuts to essential spending (staff, inventory) → risks harming operations
>     - Some costs (rent, utilities) are fixed and cannot be fully reduced
> - **\$1 million injection of capital in July**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - One-off \$1 000 k boost → July closing balance rises to \$1 600 k → strong cushion before downturn
>     - Covers shortfalls in Aug–Dec without changing day-to-day operations
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Does not address underlying cash flow issues → future months still run negative if operations unchanged
>     - Injection may come as debt or equity dilution → long-term financial cost
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - 15% reduction in outflows has the greatest impact on working capital by sustainably improving monthly net cash and reducing recurring cash deficits
>   - 20% inflow increase also helps but relies on uncertain revenue growth and may lag in effect
>   - \$1 million capital injection solves short-term gaps but fails to improve ongoing cash generation and leaves future deficits untouched

**Extract:**

**Heartfelt Greetings Ltd (HGL)**

Heartfelt Greetings Ltd (HGL) is a private limited company that designs and manufactures greetings cards in Country Y. Established 15 years ago, HGL has become known for its high-quality, hand-finished cards. The company employs 50 people and had sales revenue of \$5 million last year, with a profit of \$750,000.

HGL's cards are sold through independent gift shops and some national retail chains in Country Y. The company is considering expanding its operations to sell cards in neighbouring countries. To do this, HGL would need to increase its production capacity and invest in new printing technology.

The greetings card market in Country Y is becoming increasingly competitive. Many customers are switching to digital cards or using social media to send greetings, which has led to a 10% decline in physical card sales over the past two years. Additionally, the cost of raw materials, particularly high-quality paper, has increased by 15% in the last year due to supply chain disruptions.

HGL's Finance Director has prepared a cash flow forecast for the next six months (see Appendix 1). The forecast shows that while the business currently has a positive cash balance, it may face cash flow problems if it proceeds with its expansion plans without careful financial management.

The Managing Director is considering two options to finance the expansion:

1. Take out a long-term bank loan of \$2 million
2. Sell 25% of the company's shares to a venture capital firm

**Appendix 1: Six-month cash flow forecast for HGL (in \$000s)**

|   | **May** | **June** | **July** | **August** | **September** | **October** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Opening balance** | 200 | 150 | 50 | (50) | (100) | 0 |
| **Cash inflows** | 400 | 350 | 300 | 400 | 500 | 600 |
| **Cash outflows** | 450 | 450 | 400 | 450 | 400 | 500 |
| **Net cash flow** | (50) | (100) | (100) | (50) | 100 | 100 |
| **Closing balance** | 150 | 50 | (50) | (100) | 0 | 100 |

Consider how the following three changes in HGL's cash flow forecast could affect the business.

- Increase cash inflows by \$100,000 per month
- Reduce cash outflows by \$75,000 per month
- Arrange an overdraft facility of \$200,000

Which change would have the greatest impact on HGL's working capital? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/heartfelt-greetings-ltd-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Increasing cash inflows by \$100,000 each month could improve HGL's working capital position. They could purchase new machines to make new types of cards **[Ap]** or use it to fund advertising to tell more people about their cards. This could help them sell more, as they're currently selling 10% fewer cards **[Ap]** than before **[An]**

HGL could try to spend \$75,000 less each month. They might pay less for supplies or find cheaper ways to make cards, though if they cut too much, their cards might not be as attractive **[An]**. Customers like HGL's cards quality, finished-by-hand cards **[Ap]** and this option risks losing an important USP that attracts customers to HGL rather than rivals **[An]**

Another option is to get a \$200,000 overdraft, which could help in July and August when they expect to be low on cash** [Ap]**. However, borrowing money doesn't fix the problem of not having enough cash coming in, and overdrafts need to be paid back with interest, increasing costs **[An]**

Adding \$100,000 more cash each month would help HGL the most** [E]**. It gives them the most extra money to use and helps them make more money, not just spend less or borrow** [E]**. Spending less money might make their hand-made cards **[Ap]** less desirable, so people might stop buying them, hurting HGL's working capital position even more **[E]**. Similarly, borrowing money with an overdraft means HGL would have to pay it back later, making their money problems worse in the future **[E]**

parts.problemMd: **Explain four** reasons why profit is important to private sector businesses.
parts.solutionMd:
Profit serves as a reward for the risks taken by entrepreneurs and investors **[K]**. Business owners invest time, money, and effort to make their business successful, and profit is their financial compensation **[An]**

Secondly, profit is a useful source of finance **[K] **for businesses. Retained profit can be used to fund the purchase of assets, pay bills, and invest in research and development, helping the business grow **[An]**

Profit is also an indicator of success **[K]**. Increasing profitability suggests that a business is being run effectively and could be an attractive investment opportunity **[An]**

>   - Profit is an indicator of success – a profitable business is likely being run efficiently and may be more attractive to potential investors or lenders
>   - Profit allows for business survival and growth – businesses that generate profit are more likely to stay open, expand, and take advantage of new opportunities

parts.problemMd: Do you think cash or profit is more important for a start-up business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Cash is vital for start-up businesses. It allows them to pay for essentials like rent, supplies and wages** [K]**. Without enough cash, a start-up might fail, even if it is making a profit on paper, though it may not be enough to encourage an entrepreneur to continue with the risk **[An]**

Profit is also important for start-ups. It shows the business is successful and has potential for growth **[K]**. Profits can be used to expand the business or attract investors. However, profits do not always mean there is cash available immediately **[An]**

For a start-up, cash is more important than profit **[E]**. Cash flow problems can quickly shut down a new business, even if it is profitable. A start-up needs cash to cover daily costs and unexpected expenses. While profit is a good long-term goal, having enough cash is crucial for a start-up to survive and eventually become profitable **[E]**

> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
>

>   - Without enough cash the business may fail [k] → even if it is profitable on paper, the start-up might not survive due to unpaid bills [an]
>   - Profit shows that the business is viable long term [k] → can be used to reinvest, expand, or attract investors to support future growth [an]
>   - Profit does not guarantee available cash [k] → for example, money may be tied up in credit sales or unpaid invoices [an]
> - Evaluation might include:
> 
>   - Cash is more important in the short term [e] → because a lack of liquidity will stop the business operating, whereas profit is more useful once survival is secure [e]
>   - Supported judgement [e]→ cash is more important at the start because survival depends on it, while profit becomes more important as the business grows [e]

Making a profit is an important reward for risk-taking and enterprise **[K]**, encouraging owners to invest. Profit can be used as a source of finance for growth and is an important indicator of success. Without profit, businesses may struggle to survive long-term **[An]**

Managing cash flow is vital, because businesses need cash to pay day-to-day costs and ensure liquidity **[K]**. Even if a company is profitable, poor cash flow can lead to problems paying suppliers or employees. Effective cash flow management ensures the business can keep running and has the opportunity to generate profits in the future **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think having a high level of non-current liabilities is always a problem for a growing business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Having a high level of non-current liabilities, like long-term loans and mortgages, can help a growing business. These loans provide money to buy new equipment or buildings **[K]**. This can mean more products and potentially higher profits can be made. Also, the interest paid on these loans might reduce the amount of tax the business has to pay **[An]**

However, high non-current liabilities can be risky. Big loan payments **[K]** can make it hard for the business to pay its bills, especially if sales do not grow as expected, which is likely to mean that suppliers will no longer provide raw materials and goods, disrupting production **[An]**

Overall, I think high non-current liabilities are not always bad for growing businesses **[E]**. The chance to grow and make more money often makes up for the risks, as long as the business is careful about managing its debt and makes sure it can always make its loan payments **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think having more current liabilities than current assets is always a problem for a growing business? **Justify** your answer.

This means the business may struggle to pay its short-term debts like supplier payments and wages **[K]**. This could lead to suppliers refusing to provide goods on credit and employees leaving, which would disrupt operations and damage the business's reputation **[An]**

However, some growing businesses might temporarily have this situation during expansion phases. They might be investing heavily in stock or have large orders coming in soon **[K]**. If the business has strong sales growth and reliable customers who will pay quickly, this temporary imbalance might be manageable and could lead to higher profits once the expansion is complete **[An]**

Overall, I think having more current liabilities than current assets is usually a serious problem for growing businesses **[E]**. While there might be short-term situations where this is acceptable, the risk of not being able to pay bills and the potential damage to relationships with suppliers and employees generally outweighs any temporary benefits from rapid expansion **[E]**

Companies with very predictable cash flows, such as subscription-based businesses, might keep working capital low to invest more in growth or return money to shareholders **[K]**. This approach can increase profitability and demonstrate efficient capital management, particularly when the business has access to credit facilities for emergencies **[An]**

Overall, I believe maintaining adequate working capital is essential for long-term business success **[E]**. While some businesses can operate efficiently with lower working capital, the security and flexibility that adequate working capital provides generally outweighs the potential benefits of operating with minimal reserves, especially given the unpredictable nature of business environments **[E]**

parts.problemMd: **Explain four** reasons why current assets are important to a business.
parts.solutionMd:
Current assets provide liquidity for day-to-day operations **[K]**. Businesses need cash and assets that can be quickly converted to cash to pay suppliers, wages, and other immediate expenses **[An]**

Secondly, current assets enable businesses to meet short-term obligations **[K]**. Having sufficient current assets ensures that a business can pay its current liabilities as they fall due, maintaining good relationships with creditors **[An]**

Current assets also support business flexibility and opportunities **[K]**. Having readily available resources allows businesses to respond quickly to unexpected opportunities or challenges without needing external financing **[An]**

Finally, current assets act as a buffer against financial difficulties **[K]**. Maintaining adequate levels of current assets helps businesses survive temporary downturns in revenue or unexpected expenses **[An]**

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

**Appendix 2 **

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of three sources of finance mentioned in the appendix that Tokumbo could use for his safari business expansion:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

Which source of finance would have the most significant impact on the statement of financial position? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)[ ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
A bank loan gives quick access to money for buying safari vehicles and equipment **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, the loan appears as a non-current liability, while the new vehicles and equipment are shown as non-current assets **[Ap]**. Fixed monthly repayments make it easier to plan cash flow **[An]**. However, interest increases expenses and reduces profit margins **[An]**. Collateral may also be required, which puts assets at risk if repayments are missed **[An]**

Share capital does not need repayment, so it helps cash flow for daily operations **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, it increases the equity section, showing that investors now own a share of the business **[An]**. No interest means more profit can be kept for reinvestment **[An]**. However, selling shares reduces Tokumbo’s control over decisions **[Ap]**. Shareholders may also expect dividends, which could reduce money available for growth **[An]**

Using retained earnings has no cost or interest, so more profit is kept in the business **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, profits are transferred within the equity section, without increasing liabilities **[An]**. Tokumbo keeps full ownership and control **[An]**. However, the amount available is limited, which may restrict expansion [An]. Using these funds also reduces cash reserves, which may cause problems in slow seasons **[An]**

A bank loan would make the biggest change overall to the statement of financial position** [E]**. It increases both liabilities and assets, creating the largest impact on the balance sheet** [E]**. Share capital only affects equity, while retained earnings just move within equity. A loan would also increase gearing, changing SA’s financial structure** [Ap]**

> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Bank loan**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Immediate access to large amounts → can purchase multiple safari vehicles quickly
>     - Interest payments are tax deductible → reduces overall tax burden
>     - Fixed repayment schedule → predictable cash flow planning
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Interest payments increase expenses → reduces net profit margins
>     - Collateral requirements → business assets at risk if cannot repay
> - **Share capital**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - No repayment obligations → improves cash flow for operations
>     - New shareholders bring expertise → potential business growth opportunities
>     - No interest costs → more profit available for reinvestment
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Ownership dilution → Tokumbo loses some control over decisions
>     - Dividend expectations → pressure to distribute rather than reinvest profits
>     - Potential conflicts → disagreements over business direction
> - **Retained earnings**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - No external costs → maximises profit retention for expansion
>     - Maintains full ownership → Tokumbo keeps complete control
>     - No debt obligations → reduces financial risk
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Limited amount available → may restrict expansion plans
>     - Reduces cash reserves → affects liquidity during quiet periods
>     - Slower expansion → competitors may gain market advantage

> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Primary market research**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Up-to-date findings about local sports → helmets can be adapted to each country’s popular games (e.g. cricket style) → higher sales potential
>     - Questions focus on sports-helmet buyers’ exact needs → data is specific and reliable → products more likely to meet customer expectations
>     - Research tracks current sporting-trend changes in each market → helps spot opportunities early
>     - Results stay private to SSE → competitors cannot copy the insights
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Interviewer bias or leading questions → answers may be distorted → wrong decisions
>     - Focus groups / interviews cost more → specialist staff need paying → higher research budget
>     - Country-wide questionnaires take time to distribute and analyse → slower launch of helmets
>   - **Secondary market research**
>   
>     - **Advantages**
>     
>       - Often cheaper than doing new surveys → cuts research costs for each target country
>       - Government or trade data shows total market size for cricket helmets → helps forecast demand across new markets
>       - Newspapers and reports reveal the economy’s health → signals whether demand is likely to grow
>       - Information is quick to obtain online → faster preliminary decisions
>     - **Disadvantages**
>     
>       - Statistics on sports like skateboarding may be outdated → misleading for today’s helmet market
>       - Publicly available data → rivals can use the same figures → no competitive edge
>       - Collected for different purposes → may not answer SSE’s specific research questions
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Primary research: best when SSE needs precise, up-to-date insight into customers’ helmet preferences in each new country
>   - Secondary research: best for quickly and cheaply measuring overall market size or economic outlook before deciding whether to enter
>   - Practical approach: start with low-cost secondary data to screen potential markets, then run focused primary research in the most promising countries to fine-tune product design and pricing

parts.problemMd:
**Extract:**

**Protective Hats (PH)**

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

Appendix 1

Advertisement for PH’s products

PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work.

We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

High quality is guaranteed.

PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

**Appendix 2**

**Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director

From: Human Resources Director

Date: 1 October 2023

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

**Appendix 3**

**PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following three methods PH uses to collect market research data.

- A focus group made up of existing customers
- An online survey with only 5 questions
- Secondary research, including government sources

Which method is most likely to ensure that accurate data is collected? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
A focus group of existing customers allows PH to gain detailed information from people familiar with their products. Customers can discuss their experiences, helping PH understand the reasons behind opinions **[An]**. However, the small sample size may not represent all potential customers of protective equipment **[Ap]**, as it is restricted to existing customers, potentially missing insights about competitors or new market segments **[An]**

An online survey with five questions can quickly reach many customers worldwide. PH already has customer email addresses **[Ap]**, making distribution easy. Results can be automatically analysed using IT, saving time and money **[An]**. However, the small number of questions limits the depth of information gathered. Some customers may rush through it, providing less thoughtful answers than in a focus group **[An]**

Secondary research from government sources is likely reliable and unbiased. It may provide free access to construction industry data **[Ap]**, reducing costs. However, the information could be outdated or too general, not specifically addressing PH's protective hat market, requiring them to carry out further primary research to fill gaps in knowledge **[An]**

The focus group is most likely to ensure accurate data collection **[E]**. While limited in size, it allows PH to gather rich, detailed feedback directly from customers who use their products. PH can probe for specifics about existing hats and requirements for new mining hats **[Ap]**, supporting product development. The interactive discussion reveals nuances that quick online surveys or general government statistics might miss **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Focus group**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Participants already use PH’s protective hats **→** give honest views on good and bad points **→** helps redesign the hat
>     - Group discussion **→** researchers hear the reasons behind each opinion **→** deeper insight
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Sample limited to current customers **→** views may be biased and ignore rivals’ products
>     - Only a few people in the room **→** not enough data for accurate decisions
>     - Hiring a specialist agency and gathering customers **→** can be slow and expensive
> - **Online survey**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Answers fed straight into a computer **→** results analysed quickly and cheaply
>     - Email link reaches many customers worldwide **→** fast response and larger sample
>     - No interviewers or postage **→** costs less than face-to-face or postal surveys
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Only five questions **→** limits the detail of answers
>     - No one on hand to explain questions **→** risk of misunderstanding
>     - Some target customers may lack internet or ignore the email **→** results may not represent the whole market
> - **Secondary research**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Collected by experts **→** usually reliable and unbiased
>     - Often free to access **→** keeps research costs low
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Data may be out of date **→** might not show current trends in mining or construction
>     - Collected for a different purpose **→** may not answer PH’s specific questions about a new hat
>     - Publicly available **→** competitors can use the same figures, so no advantage
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Focus group: provides the most detailed feedback from real users, but its small and possibly biased sample makes results less representative
>   - Online survey: reaches far more people at low cost, yet includes limited questions and no guidance, which can reduce accuracy
>   - Secondary research: quick, cheap and reliable for broad market size, but may be outdated and too general for product design decisions

parts.problemMd: Do you think entering a growing market where there is a lot of competition is the best way for a business to expand? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:

As customers may already be loyal to other brands, it can be difficult to gain market share. This could result in lower growth than expected **[An]**

As a new theatre in a low-income area **[Ap]**, ET must understand what types of performances and prices appeal to local people and tourists, so that it can fill seats. Penetration pricing** [K]**, which is setting a lower price than competitors, should attract customers to switch** [An] **to the new business and rapidly increase a new business's sales

Cost plus pricing is the best pricing method as it ensures a new business can cover all its costs by adding a mark up **[E]**. Although the price maybe slightly higher than using alternative pricing methods, this is less important in a niche market where there are likely to be fewer substitute products **[E]**

>   - May result in a price that is too high [k]; which could limit demand in a price-sensitive market [an]
>   - Penetration pricing can attract customers quickly [k]; especially if launching into a competitive market [an]
>   - Niche markets may tolerate higher prices [k]; fewer substitutes mean less price sensitivity [an]
>   - Skimming may be suitable in niche markets [k]; helps recover development costs quickly if customers are willing to pay more [an]

parts.problemMd: Do you think competitive pricing is the best method for an established business to use? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Using competitive pricing means the established business sets a similar price to competitors** [K]** so it will not risk losing market share by setting a higher price and customers switching to substitutes **[An] **

However, the competitive price may not necessarily cover all costs of production **[K] **so the business may find it difficult to break even if the price is  not set high enough** [An]**

Competitive pricing is probably the best method for an established business with an established brand** [E]** to maintain its position in the market. It is better than losing sales revenue using price skimming, which may result in customers switching to substitute products if they feel the price is too high** [E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think adding new features to a product is the best extension strategy for a manufacturing business to use? **Justify **your answer.

There is a risk that existing customers may not like any new features that are added **[E]**, so it may be less risky and cheaper to try to find new customers in a new market as an extension strategy **[E] **rather than continue in a market with waning demand

- Pay a celebrity to open the shop

parts.solutionMd:
The "buy one, get 50% off second purchase" offer could encourage customers to buy more Beautywise jewellery **[Ap]**, increasing sales. However, it would reduce profit on the second item **[An]**. Offering "10% off everything for one week" could boost sales on all items as customers get a discount on all items they purchase. **Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)**

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

**Appendix 1 **

**Extract from SSE’s website **

**If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport.

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you.

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below.

Get the perfect fit for you!

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

**Appendix 3 **

**Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following **two **options for SSE to distribute its products in the new markets in other countries.

- Sell direct to customers using SSE’s website
- Sell to large sports retailers in other countries

Which option should SSE choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
Selling through the SSE website gives SSE full control over marketing, allowing them to build direct relationships with purchasers of bike, cricket and skateboarding safety helmets **[Ap]** and gain valuable feedback **[An]**. However, not all potential customers may be comfortable buying safety helmets online without trying them on  **[Ap] **first. SSE would have higher costs for processing individual orders, shipping small quantities, and handling returns if helmets don't fit properly **[An]**

Selling to large sports retailers, who are likely to place bulk orders, reduces SSE's distribution costs  **[An]**. Customers can try on helmets in stores to ensure proper fit [Ap] before buying, so they are likely to be satisfied with SSE's products and recommend them to others **[An]**. However, SSE would have less control over pricing and marketing, and would face direct competition from other brands on store shelves, which may mean they have to redesign packaging to stand out, increasing costs **[An]**

SSE should choose to sell through large sports retailers in new international markets **[E]**. Retailers have existing distribution networks and local market knowledge, which would reduce costs as less market research would be needed. It allows customers to try helmets for fit, which is crucial for safety equipment **[Ap]**, and likely to lead to more satisfied customers and an improved reputation **[E]**. While profit margins may be lower, higher sales volumes and lower operating costs make this the better choice for expanding into unfamiliar markets **[E]**

**Extract:**

**Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes.

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows.

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading.

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

**Appendix 2 **

**Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

**Appendix 3 **

**Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Consider the following three elements of a suitable marketing mix for CC’s new range of personalised mobile phone covers.

- Pricing method
- Method of promotion
- Place - distribution channel

**Justify **which element is the most important.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
For pricing, CC could use price skimming as its new personalised phone covers face little competition at present. High-income young people** [Ap] **may be willing to pay more to own one first. This could help CC recover development costs quickly **[An]**. However, high prices might limit the number of phone cases sold, as the number of young people with significant disposable income is likely to be small **[An]**

For promotion, CC could advertise on social media platforms popular with 18-25 year olds **[Ap]**, like Instagram. This is cost-effective for a small business with only 10 employees **[Ap]** and could help the covers go viral **[An]**. CC could also partner with influencers to reach their target market. However, social media trends change quickly, so CC may need to commit to ongoing spending on market research to stay current  **[An]**

For place, CC could sell the covers online and through an app. Young people between 18 and 25 are used to ordering goods this way. CC could also sell in shopping malls popular with higher-income young consumers **[Ap]**. However, this may increase CC's costs compared to only selling online **[An]**.

The most important element is likely promotion. Even with the right price and distribution, if young people don't know about the new covers, they won't buy them **[E]**. Effective social media promotion is crucial to build awareness and teaming with a celebrity influencer could create a buzz for this new product among CC's wealthy young target market **[Ap]**. Without strong promotion, the covers may not sell well regardless of price or where they're available. Price and place are important, but promotion drives initial awareness and interest for a new product like this **[E]**

**Examiner tips**

- This is an unusual question, as it requires you to make marketing recommendations throughout the answer, as well as providing an overall judgement
- Make a clear recommendation for each element of the marketing mix, apply your recommendation to the case study and, briefly, consider the advantages and disadvantages

**Guidance**

- This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation

  - Application [Ap]: up to 4 marks for references to the case study throughout
  - Analysis [An]: up to 4 marks for detailed chains of reasoning and effective use of terminology
  - Evaluation [E]: up to 4 marks for answers that demonstrate balance and reasoned judgement. Include reasons why alternatives are rejected

> 
> - **Pricing**
> 
>   - Price skimming → new cover, few rivals → set a high launch price that status-seeking customers are happy to pay first
>   - Cost-plus pricing → add a fixed % on top of costs → guarantees profit on every cover
>   - Competitive pricing → match existing premium brands → avoids looking either cheap or overpriced in a small market
>   - Penetration pricing → start slightly lower → win quick market share in the new age segment, then raise prices later

**Extract:** **Playsafe Playground Equipment (PPE)** Kaari has always been creative and made wooden toys for her two children when they were young. Her children are now at school, so Kaari decided to start her own business making wooden playground equipment. Kaari started PPE as a sole trader business three years ago in country Z. She wants an income from the business but also wants to spend time with her children. Kaari wants the business to remain small. However, if the business grows Kaari may need to change to another type of business organisation. Kaari carries out all the management roles in the business. Kaari uses job production to produce high quality, individually designed playground equipment. Kaari designs all the equipment herself and she employs 3 skilled workers to help her make the products. PPE currently makes both large and small items of playground equipment each week. Kaari uses cost-plus pricing as every item of playground equipment uses different quantities of raw materials. She sells small items of playground equipment to retailers and large items of playground equipment to the Government. There are many competitors in this market. Kaari plans to obtain new machinery which will cost \$20 000. She is considering using crowd-funding as this is one way to raise capital for new business investment. Other options include leasing the machinery or asking the bank for a loan. Kaari has developed a new unique product this year. There are no other similar products in the market. **Appendix 1** **Advertisement for PPE** Buy your playground equipment from us. At PPE we manufacture high quality playground equipment and have better designs than our competitors. All our equipment has been fully tested and is guaranteed to meet legal safety standards. We are the main supplier of playground equipment to the Government for public parks - so you know our equipment can be trusted! Contact us today for a price list. **Appendix 2** **Cost and revenue information for PPE in 2021** | | **Small item of playground**

**equipment** | **Large item of playground**

**equipment** | |---|---|---| | Average selling price | \$100 | \$1 000 | | Average cost of manufacture | \$25 | \$500 | | Output each week | 15 | 3 | **Appendix 3** **Newspaper article – Main News 1st October 2021** **Children need to get more exercise and play outside** Research suggests that playing outside helps children relax after school and improves their health. The Government in country Z has allocated \$10m to spend on improving children’s playgrounds in public places. This means there will be \$5 000 to spend on equipment for each public playground. Retailers have reported increasing demand for small items of playground equipment as parents want to have these products at home. This trend is expected to continue. Consider the following **three **pricing methods PPE could use when launching its new product. - Cost-plus - Penetration - Skimming Which pricing method should it use? **Justify **your answer. Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2021-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Cost-plus pricing has the advantage of ensuring PPE covers its costs and makes a profit on each item sold. Kaari already uses this method, and it works well for custom-made equipment **[Ap]**. However, for a new product, it doesn't consider what customers are willing to pay or how competitors price their products, which may mean that PPE's products are considered poor value compared to those of rivals **[An]**

Penetration pricing  could help PPE's new product become established in the playground equipment **[Ap] **market, where there are many competitors. The low price would attract customers and potentially lead to high sales volumes. However, PPE may not make much profit per unit sold initially, which Kaari might see as too much of a risk, given that she has unlimited liability **[Ap] **and would have to cover any losses herself **[An]**

Price skimming involves setting a high initial price. This could work as PPE's product is new and unique with no direct competitors yet **[Ap]**. It would allow PPE to make high profits initially and enhance its reputation for high quality, individually designed playground equipment **[Ap]**. However, the high price may discourage customers from buying the new product and PPE may not be able to recover product development costs **[An]**

Overall, as long as Kaari is in a position to cover any losses, I recommend penetration pricing for PPE's new product launch **[E]**. The low price will help it gain market share quickly in the competitive playground equipment industry **[Ap]**. Retailers have reported increasing demand for small items of playground equipment **[Ap]**, so a low price could help PPE take advantage of this trend. Price skimming and cost-plus pricing risk alienating lower-income customers **[E]**. While profits per unit may be lower initially, gaining customers now could lead to long-term success for this new product **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think break-even analysis is always useful to managers in decision making? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
On the positive side, break-even analysis provides clear financial targets **[K]** by showing exactly how many units need to be sold to cover costs, helping managers make informed pricing and production decisions **[An]**

It also simplifies complex financial information into easy-to-understand calculations **[K]** which enables quick comparisons between different business options and supports strategic planning **[An]**

However, break-even analysis assumes that costs and prices remain constant **[K]** which is unrealistic in dynamic markets, leading to inaccurate predictions and poor decision making **[An]**

It also ignores external factors like competitor actions and market conditions **[K]** which can significantly impact sales volumes, making the analysis less reliable for long-term planning **[An]**

Overall, break-even analysis is most useful for short-term operational decisions where variables are relatively stable **[E]**. However, for strategic long-term decisions involving market uncertainty, managers should combine break-even analysis with other tools like market research and scenario planning. This balanced approach ensures more comprehensive decision making **[E]**

>   - Explain why this reason helps decision making (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark

>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
>

> 
>   - Easy to calculate and understand [k] so saves time in decision making [an]
>   - Only considers financial factors [k] so may ignore qualitative aspects [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Break-even analysis assumes costs remain constant [k] which is unrealistic in volatile markets [an]. However, it provides clear targets [k] helping managers set realistic sales goals [an].
>   - Break-even analysis is not always useful as it oversimplifies complex business situations [eval].
>   - It works best for short-term decisions where variables are stable, but strategic decisions require additional analysis tools [eval]
> - The answer must focus on the usefulness of break-even analysis in decision making so do not accept general points about break-even analysis unless clearly linked to decision making

- Reducing variable costs
- Increasing selling price

parts.solutionMd:
Reducing variable costs would help SSM achieve break even by lowering the cost per unit of soap powder produced. SSM could negotiate better prices for raw materials or improve production efficiency to reduce waste. This would decrease the variable cost per unit, meaning fewer units need to be sold to cover total costs and reach break even point. Given SSM's worsening cash flow position, reducing variable costs would directly improve profitability on each unit sold.

Increasing selling price would raise the contribution per unit, reducing the number of units SSM needs to sell to break even. However, in the competitive soap powder market, price increases risk losing customers to competitors. SSM would need to ensure any price rise doesn't significantly reduce demand, as this could actually move the business further from break even if sales volume falls too much.

Reducing fixed costs would lower SSM's break even point by decreasing the total costs that must be covered. This could involve reducing overheads like rent, salaries, or administrative expenses. However, with the planned £15 million factory expansion, SSM's fixed costs are likely to increase rather than decrease in the short term.

Reducing variable costs is likely to have the greatest effect on SSM achieving break even. As a manufacturer using flow production to make soap powder, variable costs represent a significant proportion of total costs. Small reductions in variable costs per unit multiply across SSM's large production volumes, creating substantial savings. Unlike price increases, cost reductions don't risk losing customers in the competitive market. While fixed cost reductions help, they're harder to achieve given SSM's expansion plans and may compromise long-term growth.

**Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

**Appendix 2 **

**Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

**Appendix 3 **

**Information on three possible locations for the new shop**

| **Annual costs** | **Town A** | **Town B** | **Town C** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shop rent | \$45 000 per year for 5 years | \$35 000 per year for 10 years | \$20 000 per year for 15 years |
| Wages and salaries | \$80 000 | \$70 000 | \$60 000 |
| Heating and lighting | \$5 000 | \$5 000 | \$3 000 |
| Estimated gross profit | \$400 000 | \$300 000 | \$200 000 |

Note: Franchise fee is \$50 000 per year and 20% of gross profit is paid to Beautywise.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the **three** towns for the new shop shown in Appendix 3. Recommend which town Gemma should choose for the location of the new shop. **Justify **your answer.

parts.solutionMd:
Town A has the highest estimated gross profit at \$400,000 **[Ap]**, which would allow Gemma's Jewels to pay the franchise fee and still make a healthy profit **[An]**. However, it also has the highest rent at \$45,000 per year and the shortest lease of only 5 years **[Ap]**. The wages and heating costs are also highest here, leading to total costs of \$130,000 per year **[Ap]** before franchise payments. These factors are a risk if the business takes time to establish itself **[An]**

Town B offers a balance between profit potential and costs. The estimated gross profit of \$300,000 **[Ap]**  is less than Town A but still substantial **[An]**. The rent of \$35,000 per year for a 10-year lease **[Ap]** provides more stability than Town A. Wages are \$10,000 lower than Town A, and total costs before franchise payments are \$110,000 per year **[Ap]**. This could allow for steady growth over time.

Town C has the lowest estimated gross profit at \$200,000 **[Ap]**, but also the lowest costs. The rent is only \$20,000 per year for a long 15-year lease **[Ap]**, providing the most stability. However, the lower gross profit means less money to cover the franchise fee and other costs, potentially limiting profitability **[An]**

Gemma should choose Town B **[E] **as it provides the best opportunity for sustainable growth. It offers good profit potential, has manageable costs and a reasonable lease length **[E]**. Town A's higher costs and short lease **[Ap] **make it too risky, while Town C's lower sales potential **[Ap]** could make it difficult to be profitable after franchise payments **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think flow production is the best method of production for a manufacturing business to use? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Flow production allows for high output, helping businesses meet large demand efficiently **[K]**. Flow production also benefits from economies of scale and it's often more capital intensive, leading to lower unit costs. This can give the business a competitive advantage as these lower costs can be passed on to consumers as lower prices **[An]**

However, flow production  requires a large capital investment upfront, which not all businesses can afford. If one machine breaks down, the whole production line stops **[K]**, potentially causing significant drops in output. This may mean that business cannot meet deadlines for orders, and its customers may buy from a rival instead **[An]**

For manufacturing businesses producing standardised products with high, consistent demand, flow production is likely the best method. It allows them to maximise efficiency and minimise costs **[E]**. However, for businesses with varied product lines or fluctuating demand, batch or job production may be more suitable. The choice ultimately depends on the nature of the product, market demand, and available capital **[E]**

**Extract:** **MainCity Bakery (MB)** MainCity Bakery (MB) MB is a small bakery that produces bread. Yasin started the bakery 6 months ago with help from the government. Yasin needed a business plan to support his application for government help. An extract from the business plan Yasin produced is shown in Appendix 1. The market research was carried out by Yasin. He asked a small sample of family and friends to fill in a questionnaire. Yasin’s business plan also contained forecast data. MB’s bread is freshly-made every day in the bakery, which is located at the back of MB’s small shop. The bread is then sold the same day. Yasin has 2 employees to help him produce the bread and 1 employee to serve customers in the shop. All employees work 5 days a week and are paid the legal minimum wage. Yasin uses a democratic leadership style. Yasin needs to keep costs low to be competitive. He uses packaging that cannot be recycled. Yasin also buys the cheapest ingredients, most of which are imported. He is planning to use lean production in the bakery but he has to decide which method to use. MB’s main competitors advertise that they only use ingredients from local suppliers. Yasin is thinking of changing the suppliers he uses for ingredients and packaging. He wants MB to have a good ethical image which he could use in advertising. Yasin plans to start making cakes. He is considering two options as outlined in Appendix 2. MB’s fixed costs will increase as there will be additional expenses whichever option he chooses. **Appendix 1 ** **Extract from Yasin’s business plan for MB** | Section | Details | |---|---| | Market research | Questionnaire results are as follows:

- Bread is eaten by all age groups
- Of the sample asked:
- 85% want products made using ingredients from local suppliers
- 70% want to purchase cakes as well as bread from a bakery | | Resources | - \$10 000 to buy bakery equipment
- Rent for the bakery and shop each month
- \$3000 for start-up supplies and ingredients | **Appendix 2** **Forecast data for MB’s cake options** | | **Option 1 Small cupcakes** | **Option 2 Large birthday cakes** | |---|---|---| | Monthly sales of cakes | 4000 | 100 | | Variable cost per cake | \$0.50 | \$10 | | Additional fixed cost per month | \$3000 | \$3000 | | Price per cake | \$2 per cupcake | \$60 per birthday cake | | Gross profit margin | 75% | 83.33% | | Sales growth | Low | High | **Appendix 3 ** **Packaging supplier advertisement** We only supply packaging made from sustainable sources. This will keep your products fresh and protect the environment. We can deliver your packaging when you need it. Consider the following **two **ways MB could achieve lean production. - Kaizen. - Just-in-time inventory control. Which is the best way for Yasin to choose? **Justify **your answer. Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2022-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Kaizen could involve Yasin and his two bakery employees constantly looking for ways to improve how they make bread **[Ap]**. For example, they might reorganise the small bakery** [Ap] **layout to reduce wasted movement between tasks, increasing productivity. This would allow them to make more bread each day, potentially increasing revenue **[An]**. However, Kaizen requires everyone to be motivated to suggest improvements. Yasin's minimum wage employees **[Ap]**, may not want to help if it means their hours get reduced due to increased efficiency **[An]**

Just-in-time inventory control would involve Yasin only ordering ingredients like flour **[Ap] **when needed. This could reduce storage costs in MB's small shop and bakery area and ensure ingredients are always fresh. As MainCity Bakery makes bread daily to sell in their shop, JIT could work well with this production cycle **[An]**. However, delays in ingredient deliveries could disrupt bread production and lead to lost sales **[An]**, which is risky for such a new business focused on increasing revenue **[Ap]**

Just-in-time inventory control is the best option **[E]**. As a small bakery making products daily, reducing storage while ensuring freshness is crucial **[E]**. While Kaizen could bring benefits, it may be harder to implement with just three employees who might resist changes **[E]**. JIT aligns with MainCity Bakery's production cycle and its need to keep costs low as a new business that received government help **[Ap]** to start up. Yasin should focus on building relationships with suppliers to make JIT work effectively, which could also help improve MB's ethical image **[Ap]** by sourcing local ingredients **[E]**

> 
> - **Kaizen**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Staff suggest tiny changes **→** smoother flow in the bakery **→** less wasted time and ingredients
>     - Shorter gaps between mixing → baking → cooling **→** higher output per hour
>     - Fewer half-finished trays lying around **→** tidier workspace and lower waste

>     - Rearranging ovens and benches costs time or cash—hard for a start-up

>     - After the easy wins, further gains get smaller

>

**Extract:**

**Protective Hats (PH)**

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for PH’s products**

PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work.

We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

High quality is guaranteed.

PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

**Appendix 2**

**Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director

From: Human Resources Director

Date: 1 October 2023

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

**Appendix 3 **

**PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

Consider the following** two** ways PH could ensure quality production.

- Quality control
- Quality assurance

Which way should PH choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
Quality control could benefit PH by allowing end-of-process checks on their protective hats for construction sites, factories, and mines **[Ap]**. This method might be less expensive, which is important given PH's decreased profit margin **[An]** from 20% to 16% **[Ap]**. However, it could lead to more waste if faulty hats are rejected at the end of production, increasing costs **[An]**

Quality assurance aligns with PH's need for consistently high-quality safety equipment, with workers identifying and correcting issues at each stage. High quality output, delivered by all staff, could help PH maintain its market leader position **[Ap]** and support international expansion plans **[An]**. However, quality assurance would require employee training, slowing down production **[An]**

PH should choose quality assurance over quality control. While it may take time, it's better suited to maintaining the high standards required for safety equipment** [E]**. This method would help PH uphold its quality reputation **[Ap]**. Quality control, despite being cheaper and quicker to implement, doesn't offer the same level of consistency **[E]**, which is essential for a company producing safety-critical items for hazardous work environments **[Ap]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Quality control**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Final checks catch faulty hats before they reach customers → reduces risk of selling defective products
>     - No extra training needed for 100 line workers → inspectors handle all checks
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Must hire inspectors → adds staffing cost
>     - Finds faults only at the end → doesn’t pinpoint where errors occur → waste from scrapping/reworking remains
>     - Workers may feel untrusted → less ownership of quality → careless mistakes rise
> - **Quality assurance**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Checks built into every stage → errors caught immediately → fewer faulty hats at the end
>     - Cuts customer complaints and lowers scrap costs → boosts reputation for reliable protection
>     - Empowers workers → feels trusted → may raise motivation and care
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Training all workers in quality checks → time and expense up-front
>     - Slows production as each stage pauses for inspection → output rate may drop
>     - Only approved suppliers allowed → may limit choices and raise material costs
>     - Staff may demand higher pay for extra duties → wage costs increase
> - **Conclusion **
> 
>   - Quality control: faster to start, with minimal worker training, but only fixes faults at the end and adds inspector wages
>   - Quality assurance: prevents defects continuously, cuts waste and customer returns, yet requires investment in training, may slow output and raise costs
>   - PH should weigh how critical zero-defect reliability is versus the extra time and cost of full-process quality checks

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

**Appendix 3**

**Daily News **

**September**

**New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

State the advantages and disadvantages of the following** three** ways to achieve good quality service at the health spa:

- only employ highly trained workers
- record all customer complaints
- buy only the best quality materials to use in the health spa.
