parts.solutionMd:
Only employing highly trained workers would help ensure customers receive expert beauty treatments **[Ap]**, leading to higher satisfaction and the likelihood they will return in the future **[An]**. As Bethany already employs two qualified workers **[Ap]**, this approach aligns with her current practices. However, highly skilled staff expect to be well-paid, which could increase BB's costs **[An]**

Recording all customer complaints would help Bethany identify and address issues quickly, showing that Bethany cares about their experience **[An]**. For example, if clients complained about outdated equipment **[Ap]**, BB could consider upgrading. However, it's time-consuming and not all unhappy customers will provide feedback**, **so Bethany may not have the full picture to make important decisions **[An]**

**Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes.

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows.

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading.

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

**Appendix 2 **

**Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

**Appendix 3 **

**Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Explain the benefits and limitations of the following two ways of achieving quality production.

- Quality control
- Quality assurance

Which way should CC use? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
Having inspectors check the mobile phone covers **[Ap]** at the end of production would catch faulty covers before they reach customers, protecting CC's reputation **[An]**. The ten production workers wouldn't need extra training, as inspectors would do the checking. However, quality control could increase costs for CC as they'd need to employ specialist inspectors **[An]**. If faulty covers are only found at the end, CC might waste materials and time making personalised products **[Ap]** they can't sell **[An]**

With quality assurance, problems could be spotted early, reducing waste and saving CC money in the long run **[An]**. It might also make workers feel more motivated, as they all have a responsibility for quality **[An]**. However, quality assurance would require training all ten workers **[Ap] **to check their own work, taking them away from production. Even after training, production of phone covers might slow down if workers are constantly checking for quality **[An]**

I recommend CC use quality assurance **[E]**. It may cost more to train workers initially, but should save money over time by reducing waste. Quality assurance fits well with CC's plan to make personalised covers **[Ap]**, as each stage of production for these unique items needs careful checking **[E]**. Quality control might lead to more wasted materials and time, which a new business **[Ap]** like CC can't afford **[E]**

>

parts.problemMd: Do you think sustainable production methods are the best approach for a manufacturing business to adopt? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Sustainable production methods help businesses reduce their environmental impact **[K]**, which can improve their brand reputation and attract environmentally conscious consumers, potentially increasing sales and market share **[An]**

Sustainable production can also lead to long-term cost savings through reduced waste and more efficient use of resources **[K]**, helping businesses lower their operating costs and improve profitability over time **[An]**

However, implementing sustainable production methods often requires significant upfront investment in new technology and equipment **[K]**, which may strain the business's cash flow and reduce short-term profits **[An]**

For manufacturing businesses operating in markets where consumers value environmental responsibility, sustainable production is likely the best approach **[E]**. It allows them to differentiate their products and build customer loyalty whilst reducing long-term costs **[E]**

However, for businesses with limited capital or operating in price-sensitive markets, traditional production methods may be more viable in the short term. The choice ultimately depends on the target market, available resources, and long-term business strategy **[E]**

parts.problemMd: **Explain four **effects of training on a business.
parts.solutionMd:
Training can increase employee motivation **[K]**. When workers learn new skills, they often feel more valued and work harder** [An]**

Training can improve productivity **[K]**. Employees who know how to do their jobs well can complete tasks faster and with fewer mistakes **[An]**

Training can lead to better quality products or services **[K]**. Well-trained staff are more likely to meet customer needs by producing high quality work **[An]**

Training can create a more flexible workforce **[K]**. Employees who have a wider range of skills can be moved between different tasks as needed **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant effects might include:
> 
>   - Greater motivation of employees – work harder to produce output
>   - More flexible workforce – employees can be moved between tasks as necessary
>   - Increased productivity/efficiency – lower unit costs
>   - Quality of the product may be improved – greater customer satisfaction /improved brand image / improved reputation
>   - Employees able to use new technology – easier to introduce new equipment to speed up production
>   - Improves customer service – if trained how to answer customer queries
>   - Fewer mistakes as employees are trained – less waste/less repair costs
>   - Workforce is more knowledgeable/skilled – able to complete tasks more effectively
>   - Output lost whilst training employees – higher costs
>   - Employees may expect higher pay increasing wage costs as a result of being trained – lower motivation if pay is not increased
>   - Training costs are incurred by the business – higher costs for the business may lead to lower profit initially
>   - Employees may leave the business after they have been trained – therefore increases recruitment costs

parts.problemMd: Do you think an organisation should always use external recruitment when recruiting skilled employees? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
External recruitment provides a wider pool of applicants for a business to select the candidate with the most attractive range of new skills, experience and ideas to work in the business **[K]**. This may help a business become more innovative, efficient and competitive, as these skills and characteristics help a business to develop. **[An]**

Internal recruitment can motivate existing staff by offering promotion opportunities **[K]**. This could lead to better employee retention and reduced absenteeism, reducing business costs **[An]**

The best approach to recruitment depends on the specific situation **[E]**. If the required skills don't exist within the company, external recruitment is necessary. However, if suitable candidates are available internally, this could be quicker and more cost-effective **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - External recruitment:
>   
>     - Bring in new skills / ideas [k] which could help improve productivity /effectiveness / efficiency of business [an]
>     - Can bring in valuable knowledge and experience of competition [k] gaining a competitive edge [an]
>     - Wider choice of applicants [k] increases possibility of finding best person for job [an]
>     - No knowledge of how business works / current operations [k] so might need induction training [an]
>     - Avoids risk of upsetting employees when someone internal is promoted [k]
>     - Higher recruitment costs [k]
>     - More time spent / takes longer to fill vacancy [k]
>     - Required if no suitable candidates in the business [k]
>   - Internal recruitment :
>   
>     - Can help motivate other employees [k] which could lead to fewer people leaving / reduce absenteeism [an]
>     - Internal promotion can create another vacancy that then needs to be filled [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
>   - Justification might include:
>   
>     - External recruitment can bring in new skills and ideas [k] helping improve productivity [an]. Whereas using internal recruitment can help motivate other employees [k] which could lead to fewer people leaving [an]. Overall, it depends on the skills within the business because if there are no suitable workers external recruitment would be the only choice. [eval] [eval]
> - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
> - Advantages of external recruitment can be disadvantages of internal but do not award the same point twice as mirror answers are not accepted

parts.problemMd: Do you think off-the-job training is the best method of training for a service sector business to use? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Off-the-job training allows employees to learn without disrupting work while gaining new skills from experts outside of the business** [K]**. This can give them confidence and may increase their motivation, as the business they work for has invested money in their development. This may increase their loyalty and improve their ability to deliver good customer service **[An]**

On-the-job training could, though, be better for service businesses. Employees can keep working while learning **[K]** so productivity isn't lost, learning exactly how the business wants things done, as training is focused on skills needed for their specific role **[An]**

The best approach, in most cases, is to combine both on-the-job and off-the-job methods **[E]**. Some off-the-job training brings in new ideas, while on-the-job reinforces learning in the real work environment, delivering excellent customer service. A business should consider its specific needs, budget and the skills required when deciding on the most appropriate training methods to use **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Off-the-job:
>   
>     - Allows for mistakes to be made when learning [k] lower risk of damaging reputation [an]
>     - Up to date/new skills can be gained [k]
>     - Skills might not be available in the business [k] so benefit from new techniques/ideas [an]
>     - Use specialists/expert trainers [k] is expensive/ increases costs [an]
>     - Travel costs [k] increasing cash outflows [an]
> - Other options include:
> 
>   - On-the-job training [k]
>   
>     - Employees can carry on working [an] so some work is done [an]
>     - Control what is taught/employees learn exact way business wants things done [an] so workers only learn skills needed [an]
>     - Cheaper (than off-the-job) [an] reducing (training) costs [an]
>     - Reinforce errors/bad habits of trainer [an] reducing sales/damaging reputation [an]
>     - Trainer is less productive when training others [an]
>   - Induction training [k]
>   
>     - Only suitable for new employees [an]
>     - Help learn culture [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Off-the-job training allows employees to make mistakes when learning [k] so less likely to waste resources when working [an]. Another method is on-the-job training [k] which is cheaper [an]. Off-the-job training is better especially for a service sector business because fewer mistakes can help protect the business reputation [eval] leading to extra customers helping cover the additional costs of the training [eval]
> - Some points can be awarded as knowledge or analysis but do not award the same point twice
> - The advantage of one method can be written as a disadvantage of another method but only award once

parts.problemMd: Do you think experience is the most important factor for a business to consider when recruiting a new manager? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Experience is an important factor when recruiting a new manager, but it may not be the most important. An experienced person is likely to make fewer mistakes **[K]**, allowing the business to provide better service and increase brand loyalty. Experience shows they have the ability to do the job, potentially lowering training costs and time **[An]**

Other factors to consider include qualifications, which show technical ability, and personality **[K]**, as managers must be able to lead and work with subordinates in order for the business's objectives to be met **[An]**

Overall, experience is possibly the most important factor **[E]**, as it shows proven ability, allowing the new manager to add value quickly**. **While experience clearly demonstrates job capability, qualifications indicate knowledge and potential, which could be developed anyway with a candidate with experience **[E]**

**Extract:**

Cell Covers (CC)

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes.

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows.

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading.

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News**

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now  growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

**Appendix 2 **

**Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

**Appendix 3 **

**Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following **three **methods of employee selection. Which method should CC use when recruiting production workers? **Justify **your answer.

- Application form
- Interview
- Aptitude tests

parts.solutionMd:
Application forms provide detailed information for comparing candidates' qualifications to operate CC's new production equipment **[Ap]**. However, reviewing forms is time-consuming, and applicants may not be entirely truthful about their skills, which may lead to CC appointing the wrong applicant **[An]**

Interviews allow Aisha to assess applicants' personalities face-to-face. This is crucial, as CC needs team players to work alongside the existing ten production line workers **[Ap]**. Interviews also let applicants ask questions, ensuring they understand the job requirements before they accept the job **[An]**. However, they do not allow candidates to demonstrate practical production line skills **[An]**

Aptitude tests show if applicants can perform the job effectively, which is important for operating CC's machinery efficiently **[An]** . They can show how well candidates interact with the other skilled workers **[Ap]**. However, they may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn skills for CC's new production process **[Ap] **which is likely to be somewhat different to allow for personalisation** [Ap]**

CC should use interviews as the primary selection method **[E]**. This will allow them to assess teamwork skills and explain the requirements for producing both standardised and new personalised phone covers **[Ap]**. As the involve face-to-face interaction, Aisha may find interviews an effective way to identify workers who will fit into CC's factory environment, collaborate well with current employees, and contribute to efficient production **[E]** as the business grows **[Ap]**. This is not possible with a written application form **[An]**. As aptitude tests may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn new skills for the different production processes CC intends to introduce, they will not give Aisha all of the information she needs to make the best choice  **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Application form**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Wide range of written information on each applicant **→** quicker first screen than interviewing everyone
>     - Forms can be laid side-by-side **→** makes it easier to compare candidates fairly
>     - Lists qualifications needed to run the machines **→** CC can see straight away who is trainable
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Takes time to read every form **→** slows the hiring process
>     - Applicants can exaggerate or lie **→** risk of short-listing the wrong people
> - **Interview**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Face-to-face meeting shows personality **→** judge whether the candidate will fit into a production-line team
>     - Lets managers test teamwork and communication skills **→** higher future motivation
>     - Applicants can ask questions **→** lowers the chance they quit soon after hiring
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - More time-consuming and costly than reading forms
>     - Confident talkers may impress even if their skills are weak **→** possibility of a poor hire
> - **Aptitude test**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Measures practical ability to operate equipment **→** candidates cannot fake skill
>     - Helps pick the most skilful worker **→** higher productivity and lower unit costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Tests can be expensive and time-consuming to design and run
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Application forms: a cheap, written record for easy comparison, but the information can be false and takes time to read
>   - Interviews: reveal personality and team fit, yet they are slower and may favour confident speakers over truly skilled workers
>   - Aptitude tests: hard proof of machine-handling skills, but they add cost and extend the recruitment timeline
>   - A balanced approach could be: application forms for short-listing → brief interviews for team fit → a short aptitude test before the final offer to combine speed, fairness and reliability

parts.problemMd:
**Extract:**

**Furniture Outdoors (FO)**

FO has been a private limited company for 20 years. It is owned and run by the Chan family and is located in country Z. In country Z the secondary sector has become relatively more important as the country has developed. FO is a manufacturer of wooden furniture that is suitable for outdoor use. Its products include tables, chairs and other outdoor furniture.

Customers order online from the FO website. The furniture is then delivered to customers in country Z using FO’s own delivery vehicles. However, FO is considering changing to selling its furniture through either wholesalers or large retailers in country Z.

The Chan family have the business objective of contributing to sustainable development. FO only uses sustainably sourced wood when making furniture. This is from local forests in country Z and the wood is more expensive than imported alternatives.

For many years FO shareholders have reinvested profits to provide the finance for growth. FO recently took over 2 other furniture businesses in country Z and plans further takeovers. The Chan family plan to continue to control and manage FO after this expansion. The leadership style of these two companies is very different to that of FO and their factories are located several miles away from FO in different regions of country Z.

FO need to manage all its resources effectively. It tries to use the same components such as nails, brackets and paint for all its furniture designs. It is important to not run out of raw materials and so orders to suppliers must be carefully planned to avoid late deliveries. FO want to keep wastage of materials to a minimum. FO also need to consider how many employees are required to complete each order.

**Appendix 1 - FO website advertisement**

**FO - the only business to go to when you need new outdoor furniture for your garden. **

FO produce a range of high quality furniture to meet all your needs for fashionable, well designed outdoor furniture. Be reassured our furniture is only made from the highest quality wood from sustainable forests.

Our furniture is only available online so order today and have your furniture delivered in the next few weeks. Email any questions to us and we will reply quickly.

**Appendix 2**

**Extract of cost, selling price and sales data for one of FO’s products**

| **Fixed cost per month** | \$10 000 |
|---|---|
| **Variable cost per table** | \$125 |
| **Selling price per table** | \$250 |
| **Forecasts sales for tables per month** | 100 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Newspaper article from the Daily News April 2021 **

**Sustainable production needed to save the planet **

A report from the International Committee for the Planet states that manufacturers must find more sustainable ways to produce their products as global warming is becoming more of an issue.

The report suggests three main ways manufacturers can change:

- Only use raw materials from sources that replace what they have used. This is estimated to raise variable costs by 20%
- Only use packaging that can be recycled. Costs are estimated to increase but the selling price may not rise by more than 10%
- Only use electric vehicles to deliver products. The cost of buying electric vehicles is more than petrol or diesel vehicles. Using electric vehicles could enable variable costs to be reduced by 5%.

Consider the benefits and limitations of the following **three **methods of communication FO could use.

- Email
- Mobile (cell) phone
- Letter

Which method of communication would be most suitable when contacting suppliers about a late delivery? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-june-2021-insert-paper-2-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Email is quick and can reach multiple suppliers at once. FO could easily send details about missing wood, nails or paint **[Ap] **to several suppliers. However, emails may go unread or end up in junk folders, potentially delaying responses about late materials **[An]**

Mobile phones allow for immediate two-way communication. FO could call suppliers to urgently discuss late deliveries of brackets or other components needed for manufacturing outdoor furniture **[Ap]**. However, it may be time-consuming to reach the right person, especially if FO needs to contact multiple suppliers about various raw materials **[An]**

Letters provide a formal record, which could be useful if there are ongoing issues with late deliveries affecting FO's production schedule and it needs to seek compensation **[An]**. However, letters are slow, which is problematic when FO needs materials quickly to fulfil its online **[Ap]** customer orders **[An]**

Email would likely be most suitable for contacting suppliers about late deliveries **[E]**. It balances speed and detail, so FO can quickly send specific information about missing materials to multiple suppliers. This is crucial, as FO needs to manage its resources carefully to avoid production delays and ensure online customers **[Ap]** receive orders promptly **[E]**. While a phone call might be faster for a single supplier, email is more efficient for contacting several suppliers about various late materials. Email also provides a written record FO can reference, unlike phone calls **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Email**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Sent in seconds → suppliers get the message fast, even in another country.
>     - One click reaches many suppliers at once → saves time compared with phoning each one.
>     - Can be printed or saved → FO keeps a hard-copy record for later checks.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - No guarantee the supplier opens it **→** message may sit in a junk folder.
>     - Needs a good internet link **→** delays if the network is down.
>     - High inbox traffic **→** email could be lost among other messages.
> - **Mobile (cell) phone**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Call is heard instantly **→** FO knows the message reached the right person.
>     - Two-way conversation **→** supplier can answer questions about brackets or delivery times.
>     - Most people keep phones with them **→** easier to reach busy suppliers.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - May ring several numbers before finding the right contact **→** time-consuming.
>     - International calls and time-zone differences **→** can be costly or inconvenient.
>     - No written record **→** details could be forgotten or disputed later.
> - **Letter**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Provides a formal, signed hard copy **→** useful for legal or large orders.
>     - Plenty of space to explain problems, e.g. late nails and paint.
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Slowest method **→** may add days to order resolution.
>     - Printing and postage costs higher than email or quick calls.
>     - Still no certainty the letter is received unless sent “signed-for”.
> 
> **Conclusion**
> 
> - **Email**: best when many suppliers must be updated quickly and FO needs a written record.
> - **Mobile phone**: gives instant feedback for urgent questions but is slower for multiple suppliers and leaves no paper trail.
> - **Letter: **suits detailed or formal issues yet is too slow for day-to-day delays.
> - FO should match the method to the situation: urgent delivery queries → email or phone; formal contract changes → letter.

**Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)**

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

**Appendix 1 **

**Extract from SSE’s website **

**If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport.

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you.

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below.

Get the perfect fit for you!

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

**Appendix 3 **

**Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week.

Consider how the following **three **barriers could make communication less effective between SSE’s head office in country Z and its new factories in other countries.

- Problem with the medium used
- Problem with the sender
- Problem with the receiver

Which barrier would be the easiest to overcome? **Justify **your choice.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
A problem with the medium used could arise if SSE relies too heavily on email for urgent messages. For example, if the head office needs to quickly inform a new factory about a change in helmet design specifications **[Ap]**, an email could get lost in a spam folder or not be seen immediately. This could lead to production delays or mistakes **[An]**

The sender of messages from SSE's head office may create barriers by using technical jargon about helmet manufacturing **[Ap] **that managers in the new factories don't understand. Or they might send overly long messages with too much information, causing important points about safety standards to be overlooked and helmets failing to meet them, causing wastage **[An]**

Receivers in the new factories could cause communication problems if they don't carefully read messages from head office. They may also misinterpret instructions about helmet production targets **[Ap]** if they speak a different language and don't fully grasp the nuances, giving SSE less output to sell **[An]**

The easiest barrier to overcome is likely the problem with the sender **[E]**. SSE could provide training to head office staff in country Z **[Ap]** on writing clear, concise messages without jargon. They could also create templates for common communications such as emails or staff notices to ensure important information is highlighted. Addressing these sender issues would improve communication regardless of the medium used or receiver's situation **[E]**

> - Add a final Evaluation (E):

> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts

>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Problems with the medium used**
> 
>   - Too many links in the chain → each person may change the wording → final message is distorted
>   - Message can be lost → receiver never reads it → task (e.g. making helmets) is not done
>   - Wrong channel for the situation → slow delivery when speed is vital (letter vs phone)
>   - Technical breakdown → no internet / dead battery → message never reaches receiver
> - **Problems with the sender**
> 
>   - Unclear wording → jargon or speaking too fast → receiver misunderstands
>   - Message is overloaded → key facts about, say, cricket helmets are hidden → action not taken
>   - Sent to the wrong person or wrong file → message ignored → decision delayed

> **Conclusion**

parts.problemMd: Do you think job enrichment is a better way for a business to motivate its employees than profit sharing? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:

Overall, job enrichment is better **[E]** because it makes jobs more interesting daily, while profit sharing only happens periodically, usually once a year. parts.problemMd: Do you think performance-related pay is a better way for a business to motivate its employees than job rotation? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Performance-related pay directly links employee rewards to their individual output **[K]**. This can increase productivity as workers are incentivised to work harder knowing they will be financially rewarded for better performance. However, it may create unhealthy competition between colleagues and could demotivate lower performers who struggle to meet targets **[An]**

Job rotation prevents employees from becoming bored with repetitive tasks **[K]**. It develops a wider range of skills and keeps work interesting, which can improve job satisfaction and reduce staff turnover. However, some employees may prefer to specialise in one area and constant changes could reduce efficiency as workers need time to adapt to new roles **[An]**

Overall, performance-related pay is better **[E]** because it provides immediate financial incentives that directly reward effort and results. Job rotation may improve satisfaction but doesn't guarantee increased productivity, whereas performance-related pay creates a clear link between effort and reward that motivates employees to achieve better business results **[E]**

DEF Fashions (DEF)

DEF is a medium-sized clothing and fashion accessories manufacturer based in Country X. Established 25 years ago as a private limited company, it has grown steadily and now employs 250 people across its two factories and head office. DEF specialises in producing trendy, affordable clothing and accessories for budget high-street retailers.

The fast fashion industry has become increasingly competitive, with pressure to reduce costs and improve speed to market. DEF's sales have remained stable over the past two years, but profits have declined (see Appendix 1). The CEO is considering investing in automation technology to increase production efficiency and reduce labour costs. Staff have expressed significant concerns about this, and there have been discussions with trade unions regarding possible industrial action.

DEF currently manufactures all its products in Country X. It struggles to recruit and retain staff, and productivity is low. It is investigating the possibility of outsourcing some production to countries with lower labour costs to improve profit margins.

The government of Country X has recently introduced new regulations requiring clothing manufacturers to disclose their supply chain and ensure fair labour practices. DEF is evaluating the potential impact on its operations and relationships with suppliers.

Job rotation can reduce boredom and increase job satisfaction by adding variety, which Herzberg suggests may be a key motivator **[An]**. It may improve workers' skills and understanding of the whole production process, giving the business much-needed flexibility **[An]** as many staff leave **[Ap]**. However, it could temporarily reduce efficiency as workers learn new roles, and some employees may resist change **[An]**

Overall, DEF should implement job rotation for production workers **[E]**. This directly addresses the issue of low productivity in the factories **[Ap]**. It is likely to be less costly than profit-sharing, which is important given DEF's falling profits **[Ap]**. **Extract:**

**SunnyShade Hats (SSH)**

SunnyShade Hats is a private limited company (Ltd) that designs and makes sun hats. It started six years ago and now has 40 production workers and 8 office staff in City M. SSH sells hats on its website and to independent clothes shops. The owners, Naila and Amir, want to expand by launching a new eco-friendly range called OceanWave.

SSH currently buys most fabric from Country T and pays in US dollars (USD). Fabric prices have been stable, but transport costs are rising. The company uses industrial sewing machines. A bank loan of £300 000 was used last year to buy new machines.

Quality is very important. Recent checks show defect rates have increased as new staff have joined. SSH plans to hire 20 more machinists. Managers are deciding how to motivate staff to increase output and reduce defects. Two ideas are:

- Piece rate (a payment per hat made)
- Job rotation with extra skills training

SSH is also reviewing its packaging for online orders. The current plastic mailer is cheap and waterproof. A supplier has offered recyclable cardboard packaging that looks premium but costs more and may be less water-resistant.

To support decision making, the finance manager prepared weekly cost data and a summary of assets and liabilities for this year and last year. The marketing team has created a simple online advert for the OceanWave launch. A news article has also highlighted changes in the economy that could affect SSH.

### Appendix 1 – Online advert (draft)

**SUNNYSHADE – OCEANWAVE**
Light • durable • **made from recycled fibres**
Intro price: **£24.99**
Free head-size guide • Free returns
Follow us @SunnyShadeHats

### Appendix 2 – Statement of financial position items (end of year)

| **Item** | **2025 (£)** | **2026 (£)** |
|---|---|---|
| Inventories | 120,000 | 90,000 |
| Trade receivables | 180,000 | 210,000 |
| Cash | 40,000 | 10,000 |
| Trade payables | 160,000 | 190,000 |
| Bank overdraft | 0 | 50,000 |
| Bank loan (long term) | 300,000 | 300,000 |

### Appendix 3 – Business news (extract)

The economy is facing mixed news this month. The local currency has dropped 8% against the US dollar since January, making imports more expensive. At the same time, the government announced a 5% rise in the minimum wage to help workers cope with higher living costs. Meanwhile, the central bank cut interest rates by one percentage point in a bid to boost economic growth and encourage more borrowing and investment.

### Appendix 4 – Weekly cost and output (current line)

| **Measure** | **Value** |
|---|---|
| Output (hats per week) | 3,000 |
| Fixed costs per week | £6,000 |
| Total variable costs per week | £15,000 |

SSH wants to increase output and reduce defects. They are considering two ways to achieve this:

- Introducing piece rate pay
- Job rotation with extra skills training

Which method is more likely to work best for machinists? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2025/09/37160_Paper%202%20Set%20A%20Insert.pdf)  when answering the question.
parts.solutionMd:
Paying a piece rate for each hat produced can raise speed and earnings **[K] **and may lift weekly throughput **[Ap]**. However, because defects have already increased, piece rates can encourage rushing, leading to more errors, rework and returns, which raises unit costs and risks late orders for online customers **[An]**
Job rotation with skills training can build multi-skilled teams **[K] **that can switch between cutting, stitching and checking **[Ap]**. Training improves accuracy, reduces mistakes earlier in the process and smooths flow, so defects fall and output becomes more reliable, even if training time slows production in the short term **[An]**
Overall, job rotation with training is more likely to achieve both aims because it addresses the root cause (skills/quality) and boosts long-term productivity **[E]**. SSH could add a small output bonus on top of rotation to protect pace while maintaining quality checks. Therefore, rotation-plus-training is the stronger option for OceanWave **[E]**

**Lavelle Manoir Cleaning Products Ltd**

Lavelle Manoir Cleaning Products Ltd is a private limited company that manufactures and sells household cleaning products in Country X. The company was founded 25 years ago and has grown steadily, now employing 150 workers across two production facilities and a head office.

Lavelle Manoir's main products include all-purpose cleaners, laundry detergents, and dishwashing liquids. The company uses flow production methods, with automated production lines for each product category. Lavelle Manoir sources its raw materials from chemical suppliers in Country X and neighbouring countries.

The company has traditionally sold its products through supermarkets and independent retailers in Country X. However, changing consumer preferences for eco-friendly products and increased competition from multinational brands have led to a 15% decline in sales over the past two years. Profits have fallen from \$2.5 million to \$1.8 million during this period.

To address these challenges, Lavelle Manoir's board of directors is considering a significant strategic change. They are debating whether to invest in developing a new line of environmentally friendly cleaning products, or to expand internationally by exporting to the neighbouring Country Y.

The Managing Director, Sarah Chen, believes that developing eco-friendly products could help Lavelle Manoir attract environmentally conscious consumers and improve its brand image. However, the Production Director, John Smith, argues that international expansion would better utilise the company's existing manufacturing capacity and create new market opportunities.

Lavelle Manoir's workforce includes both skilled technicians and production line workers, with many employees having worked for the company for over a decade. The company has a relatively flat organisational structure, with just three levels of hierarchy. However, communication between departments has been identified as an area for improvement.

Recent changes in Country X's economy are also affecting Lavelle Manoir's decision-making. Interest rates have risen by 2%, and there are concerns about a potential economic downturn. Additionally, the government has introduced new regulations on chemical usage and disposal that may increase production costs for cleaning product manufacturers.

**Appendix 1: Lavelle Manoir Cleaning Products Ltd - Key Financial Data**

| **Year** | **Revenue (\$m)** | **Profit (\$m)** | **Number of Employees** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 25 | 2.5 | 160 |
| 2022 | 22 | 2.1 | 155 |
| 2023 | 21 | 1.8 | 150 |

Consider how the following three changes to Lavelle Manoir Ltd's organisational structure could improve communication between departments.

- Introducing a matrix structure
- Implementing more formal communication channels
- Delayering the organisation

Which change would be the most effective? **Justify **your choice.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/lv-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Introducing a matrix structure could help because creating cross-functional teams would allow employees from different departments like production and marketing to work together on projects, improving coordination **[An]**. However, it may cause confusion amongst Lavelle Manoir's 150 workers **[Ap] **about who is in charge of whom, slowing down decision-making **[An]**

More formal communication channels, such as regular interdepartmental meetings or a company intranet, would ensure information is shared consistently **[An]**. This could improve the poor communication between departments **[Ap]**, but it might slow down decision-making in Lavelle Manoir's two factories **[Ap]**

Delayering by removing management levels would shorten the chain of command. This could speed up communication between Lavelle Manoir's head office and the two production facilities **[Ap]**. However, with 150 employees, completely flat structures may be impractical, with workers having too little supervision **[An]**

The most effective change would be more formal communication channels **[E]** because it directly addresses Lavelle Manoir's communication issues without drastically altering the existing structure **[E]**. Regular meetings between department heads like Sarah Chen and John Smith **[Ap] **could improve coordination on key decisions **[E]**, such as whether to expand internationally **[Ap]**. Matrix structures or delayering could disrupt Lavelle Manoir's production and impact efficiency during a time of declining sales **[Ap]**. Improving formal communication channels can be gradual, allowing the company to improve coordination between departments while maintaining output **[E]**

> - **Introducing a matrix structure**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Creates cross‐functional teams → improves direct communication and collaboration between R&D, production and marketing
>     - Dual reporting lines → encourages shared responsibility and information sharing across departments
>     - Leverages specialist expertise on projects → speeds up problem solving and innovation

>   - **Advantages**

parts.problemMd: Do you think the most important purpose of business activity is always to add value? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Adding value is important if a business wants to make a profit **[K]**, as it involves increasing the difference between the costs of making a product and the price it can be sold. If a business does not make a profit, it is unlikely to survive in the long term** [An]**

Meeting customer needs **[K]** is also important. If customers are not satisfied with a business's products, they may choose to buy from competitors, reducing business sales and making it difficult to break even **[An]**

Adding value is not always the most important purpose of business activity, especially for less established business start-ups **[E]**. It is more important to meet customer needs so they buy products repeatedly. This may involve lowering prices or increasing quality, which could actually reduce added value in the short run. Once brand-loyal, adding value to make a profit may be more important to ensure the long-term survival of a business **[E]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Adding value: Increases the difference between cost of production and selling price [k]; helps the business generate profit [an]; without profit, a business may not survive in the long term [an]
>   - Meeting customer needs: Providing products or services that satisfy demand [k]; if customers are unhappy, they may switch to competitors [an]; loss of customers can reduce sales/revenue and threaten survival [an]
>   - Making a profit: Businesses need profit to reinvest, grow or reward investors [k]; no profit means the business may not be able to operate long-term [an]
>   - Survival: Especially important for new or small businesses [k]; focus might be on covering costs rather than adding value at first [an]
>   - Social/ethical aims: Some businesses prioritise sustainability or social impact [k]; these aims might reduce short-term profit or added value [an]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Adding value is important for generating profit [k]; however, for start-ups, meeting customer needs may be more important to ensure repeat sales and survival [eval]
>   - A business may need to reduce prices or increase quality to attract buyers, even if this lowers added value [eval]
>   - Once brand loyalty is built, the business can then focus more on adding value to improve profit and ensure long-term success [eval]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problemMd: Do you think land is always the most important factor of production for business success? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Land provides the physical space and natural resources needed for production **[K]**, such as raw materials, location for facilities, and access to natural resources. Without suitable land, businesses may struggle to operate efficiently or access essential inputs for their production processes **[An]**

Labour is also crucial for business success **[K]**. Skilled workers are needed to transform inputs into outputs, and without adequate human resources, even the best land and equipment cannot generate products or services that meet customer needs **[An]**

Land is not always the most important factor of production, particularly for service-based businesses or those operating in the digital economy **[E]**. For many modern businesses, skilled labour and technology may be more critical than physical location. A software company, for example, can operate successfully with minimal land requirements but needs highly skilled programmers and advanced technology. However, for manufacturing or agricultural businesses, land remains essential for providing space and raw materials needed for production **[E]**.

> - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
> - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
> - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
> - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - **Land**: Provides physical space and natural resources for production [k]; essential for manufacturing, agriculture, and retail businesses that need premises [an]; poor location can limit customer access and increase costs [an]
>   - **Labour**: Skilled workers transform inputs into outputs [k]; without adequate human resources, production cannot take place effectively [an]; skilled labour can increase productivity and quality [an]
>   - **Capital**: Machinery and equipment needed for efficient production [k]; modern technology can increase output and reduce costs [an]; lack of capital investment may make businesses uncompetitive [an]
>   - **Enterprise**: Entrepreneurial skills needed to combine other factors effectively [k]; without good management and decision-making, other factors may be wasted [an]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Land is crucial for businesses requiring physical premises or natural resources [k]; however, service businesses may need minimal land but require skilled labour instead [eval]
>   - Modern technology-based businesses may operate with small physical footprints but need significant capital investment [eval]
>   - The importance of each factor depends on the type of business and industry sector [eval]

**Extract:**

**Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

**Appendix 2 **

**Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

**Appendix 3 **

By setting targets like a 10% annual sales increase **[Ap]**, Gemma can track her progress over time by comparing actual sales figures to her goal **[An]**. parts.problemMd: Do you think the shareholders are the most important stakeholder group to the success of a limited company? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Shareholders provide finance to help a business expand and buy equipment **[K]**, which can increase output and ensure it meets customer demand. They can influence the company's aims **[K]**, often focusing on maximising profits over other objectives, meaning that customer needs are less central to business activities **[An]**

Other stakeholders like customers are vital too as they buy the products **[K]**. Without enough customers, revenue will not cover costs and the business would struggle to survive **[An]**

Shareholders are important as they invest money in the company, which can help it expand. However, once the company is established, they have little influence over day-to-day decisions **[E]** unless they are directors or managers. Customers always matter, as they buy the products, which determines ongoing success, so customer are probably the most important stakeholders** [E]**

> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Shareholders/owners
>   
>     - Provide finance / invest money / capital in business [k] which can help the business expand / buy more equipment [an] so can increase output [an]
>     - Influence the aims of the business [k]
>     - Have the power to vote out the directors [k]
>     - They have little / no influence over day-to-day decisions [k]
>   - Other stakeholders can include:
>   
>     - Customers [k] as they buy the products [an] and if ignores their needs the business will lose sales/revenue [an]
>     - Directors/managers [k] are responsible for day-to-day decision-making [an]
>     - Employees [k] make the products [an] so if they become demotivated quality may fall [an]
>     - Suppliers [k] provide materials/inventory [an]
>     - Local community [k] provide the workers [an]
>     - Government [k] provide the legal framework in which the business operates [an]
>     - Bank [k] provide finance/loans [an]
>   - Justification might include:
>   
>     - Shareholders are important as they invest money in the business [k] which can help the business expand [an]. However, once the business is established, they have little / no influence over day-to-day decisions
>     - Customers [k] matter as they buy the products [an]. While shareholders provide important finance, without customers even a limited company cannot generate income [eval] and without this cannot cover its costs or make a profit, so the customer is probably the most important stakeholder. [eval]

RMT Clothing Ltd is a medium-sized clothing retailer based in Country X. It was founded in 1995 and has grown to 50 stores across the country, selling affordable fashion for men and women aged 18-35. RMT currently employs 800 people, and had annual revenue of \$85 million last year.

The company is facing increasing competition from online retailers. RMT's CEO, Sarah Jones, is considering whether to close 10 underperforming stores and invest in expanding the company's e-commerce operations instead. This would involve making 100 store staff redundant but hiring 50 new employees to work on the website and in the distribution centre.

RMT's financial performance over the last 3 years is shown in table 1 below.

**Table 1: RMT’s Financial Performance 2020 to 2022**

| Year | Revenue (\$m) | Profit (\$m) | Online sales (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 80 | 4.0 | 15 |
| 2021 | 82 | 3.8 | 18 |
| 2022 | 85 | 3.5 | 22 |

The company's main stakeholders have differing views on the proposed changes. Shareholders are concerned about falling profits and want to see a clear plan for growth. Employees are worried about potential job losses. Customers have been complaining that RMT's website is difficult to use compared to competitors.

RMT is also facing external challenges including rising energy and material costs, as well as changing consumer preferences towards more sustainable fashion. However, there are opportunities to expand into new international markets through e-commerce.

Sarah needs to decide on the best strategy to ensure RMT's long-term success in a rapidly changing retail environment.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following two options for RMT to achieve its objective of improving financial performance:

- Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce operations
- Keep all stores open but reduce costs

Which option do you recommend? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/rmt-clothing-ltd-case-study.pdf) when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Online sales have been growing, reaching 22% in 2022 **[Ap]**, so RMT's customers are increasingly shopping online. Expanding e-commerce could help RMT compete better with online rivals, increasing market share **[An]**. It would also reduce costs from running physical stores, like rent and utilities, which could contribute to improving RMT's profit **[An]**. However, it would mean making 100 store staff redundant **[Ap]**, which could damage employee morale and RMT's reputation **[An]**

Keeping all stores open but reducing costs avoids job losses, which would please employees **[An]**. It maintains RMT's physical presence, which some customers prefer **[Ap]**. Costs could be reduced by negotiating better deals with suppliers, reducing inventory or cutting marketing expenses **[An]**. However, it might not improve profits enough, as RMT's profit has been declining despite increasing revenue **[An]** from \$80m to \$85m between 2020-2022 **[Ap]**

I recommend closing 10 stores and expanding e-commerce **[E]**. This recognises changing customer behaviour, with more and more buying RMT's products online **[Ap]**. While 100 jobs would be lost, 50 new jobs would be created in e-commerce and distribution **[Ap]** and there is potential to enter overseas markets by selling online **[E]**. While shareholder concerns about falling profits would be addressed by reducing costs, simply cutting costs and carrying on operating stores doesn't address the fundamental market changes and limits potential to gain new customers, especially in other countries **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce operations**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Reduces fixed costs by closing 10 underperforming stores → cuts rent and staffing expenses
>     - Frees up funds to improve the online platform and distribution centre → meets customer demand for easier web shopping
>     - Online sales have risen from 15 % in 2020 to 22 % in 2022 → aligns investment with a growing channel
>     - Focuses the store network on profitable locations → increases average revenue per remaining store
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - 100 store-staff redundancies vs only 50 new online roles → net loss of jobs may harm staff morale and public image
>     - Loss of physical presence in 10 communities → risks alienating loyal local shoppers
>     - Upfront investment needed for website upgrades and warehouse expansion → may strain cash flow in the short term
>     - Reduced ability for customers to try on products in-store → could weaken omnichannel experience
> - **Keep all stores open but reduce costs**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Protects all 800 employees’ jobs → maintains morale and local goodwill
>     - Retains full network of 50 stores → preserves brand visibility and customer convenience
>     - Cost cuts (e.g. negotiate rent reductions, streamline staffing rotas, bulk-buy supplies) → improves margins without closing sites
>     - Less disruptive for customers and staff → avoids the risks of large-scale closures
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Cost savings may be too small to reverse falling profits → limited impact on overall financial performance
>     - Risk of cutting too deeply → service levels or product quality could suffer, driving customers away
>     - Underperforming stores continue to lose money → ongoing drain on resources that could fund growth
>     - Delay in e-commerce investment → competitors may pull further ahead online
> - **Recommendation**
> 
>   - Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce is the stronger choice to improve financial performance because it delivers larger, more immediate cost savings and aligns with clear growth in online sales
>   - To balance the impact on staff and customers, RMT should offer generous redundancy packages, retrain some store staff for online roles, and maintain an omnichannel focus by enhancing click-and-collect services
>   - This strategy uses savings from store closures to fund a robust e-commerce upgrade, positioning RMT for long-term success in a digital retail environment

parts.problemMd: **Explain **four reasons for changes in the relative importance of the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in a country.
parts.solutionMd:
The importance of the secondary sector has increased because incomes have increased** [K]** so consumers have more purchasing power to buy manufactured goods **[An]**

The importance of some parts of the primary sector, such as fishing and gas extraction, has fallen as a result of resource depletion **[K]**, which has made it difficult for businesses in these sectors to make a profit **[An]**

The tertiary sector has become more important in some countries as a result of deindustrialisation** [K]**. National governments have encouraged service sector growth by investing in improved education and skills **[An]**

Increased mechanisation and use of technology **[K] **in industries such as farming have led to a decrease in employment in the primary sector **[An]**

> 
>   - Change in the primary sector – increase due to new discovery of natural resources / decreases due to depletion of natural resources
>   - Change in the secondary sector – increase due to industrialisation / decreases due to deindustrialisation
>   - Change in the tertiary sector – increase due to increased consumer incomes
>   - Increase in incomes / economic growth / increase in GDP – this could lead to a change in the secondary or tertiary sector
>   - Increase in demand for manufactured goods – increase in the size of secondary sector
>   - Increase in tertiary sector – as consumers have higher disposable income to spend on services
>   - Increased mechanisation / increased technology – reduces number of employees in the secondary sector
>   - People move into the tertiary sector to provide services – as demand for services grows as a country develops e.g. tourism
>   - Increase in exported products – more need to be manufactured in secondary sector
>   - Reduced employment in primary sector – as now primary products produced using mechanisation / rural to urban migration
>   - Primary products are now processed in own country – increased manufacturers / secondary sector to process the raw materials into finished products
>   - Government policies to encourage development
>   - Increased globalisation
>   - Actions of environmental groups / pressure groups leading to sectoral change – primary extraction or dirty manufacturing in the secondary sector

parts.problemMd: Do you think important services, such as healthcare and education, should always be provided by the public sector? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:

Significant government spending needs to be invested in them, but a healthy and educated population can lead to economic growth **[E]**. >   - Government has a duty to provide merit goods like education and healthcare [k]; without public funding, underconsumption of these essential services may occur [an]

parts.problemMd: Do you think important services, such as transport and education, should be provided by the private sector? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Private sector provision of transport and education can lead to greater efficiency and innovation **[K]**. Private companies have profit incentives to reduce costs and improve services to attract customers, which can result in better quality provision and more responsive customer service **[An]**.

However, private sector provision may create barriers to access **[K]**. Private companies focus on profitable routes or areas, potentially leaving rural or low-income communities underserved. This could lead to increased inequality as only those who can afford premium services receive quality transport and education **[An]**.

Important services should not be provided solely by the private sector, as this risks creating a two-tier system where access depends on ability to pay. While private sector involvement can bring efficiency gains, essential services like transport and education require government oversight to ensure universal access **[E]**. A mixed approach combining private efficiency with public sector regulation and funding can deliver both quality and equity, ensuring these vital services reach all citizens regardless of income level **[E]**.

> - Explain why this reason helps society (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
> - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
> - Explain why this could also impact society → 1 An mark
> - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - Private sector provision increases efficiency and innovation [k]; competition drives companies to improve services and reduce costs to attract customers [an]; this can lead to higher quality transport networks and educational outcomes [an]
>   - Private companies focus on profit maximisation [k]; this may result in cherry-picking profitable routes or wealthy students whilst neglecting less profitable areas [an]; leading to reduced access for rural or low-income communities [an]
>   - Market forces encourage responsiveness to consumer demand [k]; private providers must satisfy customers to maintain revenue [an]; resulting in more tailored and flexible service provision [an]
>   - Private sector may prioritise short-term profits over long-term social benefits [k]; essential infrastructure and education require sustained investment that may not be immediately profitable [an]
> - Justification might include
> 
>   - Private sector provision risks creating inequality of access based on ability to pay [eval]; essential services like transport and education are merit goods that benefit society as a whole and require universal provision [eval]
>   - While private sector can improve efficiency, complete privatisation may lead to market failures and exclusion of vulnerable groups [eval]
>   - A balanced approach combining private sector efficiency with public oversight ensures both quality and universal access [eval]

FBT Travel Agency 
FBT Travel Agency is a large private limited company based in Country X. Founded in 1998, it has grown from a small family-run business to a major player in the travel industry, specialising in both domestic and international travel packages. The company employs 500 people across its head office and 50 high-street branches, which are located in major cities and towns throughout Country X. FBT's core business involves creating and selling holiday packages that include flights, accommodation, and activities. It caters for various market segments, from budget travellers to luxury seekers. In recent years, FBT has also started offering cruise packages and adventure tourism options to diversify its product range. The company is considering expanding its online presence to compete with internet-based travel companies. Currently, 32% of FBT's bookings are made online, but management believes this could be significantly increased with better digital platforms and marketing. They are debating whether to close some of their physical branches and invest more in their website and mobile app. FBT is also considering diversifying into the business travel market. This would involve creating a new division to cater specifically to corporate clients, offering services such as conference bookings, group travel arrangements, and loyalty programs for frequent business travellers. The travel industry has faced significant challenges in recent years due to global events and changing consumer preferences. The COVID-19 pandemic had a particularly severe impact on FBT's operations, as shown in their financial performance over the past three years:

FBT’s Financial Performance 2020-2022 
Year Revenue (\$ million) Profit (\$ million) Number of customers (thousands) Online bookings (%) 2020 150 15 500 20% 2021 120 8 400 25% 2022 135 12 450 32%

The company faces several external challenges, including: 1. Increased competition from online travel agencies offering lower prices 2. Economic uncertainty affecting consumer spending on travel 3. Changing regulations in the tourism industry, particularly regarding sustainability 4. Rapid technological changes requiring constant updates to booking systems and platforms However, there are also opportunities, such as: 1. Growing demand for sustainable and eco-friendly travel options 2. Increasing interest in adventure tourism 3. Potential for expansion into emerging markets in neighbouring countries FBT's management team needs to make strategic decisions to ensure the company's future success in a rapidly changing market. They are particularly focused on improving their digital capabilities, streamlining their operations, and finding new ways to generate revenue

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of FBT Travel Agency expanding into the following two sectors.

parts.solutionMd:

parts.problemMd: Do you think the number of employees is the best way to measure the size of a tertiary sector business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Tertiary sector businesses provide services that are often delivered by members of staff** [K]**. Measuring the size of a tertiary business by the number of employees could be suitable because the more workers it has, the more services it can provide** [An]**

However, some tertiary businesses use technology to provide their service **[K]**. For example, supermarkets have self-service checkouts, so fewer staff are needed to serve customers. Using the number of employees would, therefore, be misleading. Measures such as the value of sales revenue may be more appropriate **[An]**

In many cases, the number of workers is an appropriate way to measure business size **[E]** but, as technology is increasingly being used to provide a service, it may be less useful in the future. Other methods, such as the value or volume of sales or even the number of outlets, could provide more precision **[E]**

parts.problemMd: Do you think being a risk-taker is a more important characteristic of a successful entrepreneur than being creative? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:

Creativity adds value to products, allowing entrepreneurs to charge higher prices. This differentiates products from competitors, crucial for success, especially in saturated markets **[An]**

Overall, creativity is likely to be most valuable. An entrepreneur can take risks, but if customers do not purchase due to a lack of innovation or differentiation, they will not be successful **[E]**.
