>   - Local suppliers may have stronger cultural understanding → brand loyalty may prevent customers from switching to SSM powder
> - **Lack of knowledge**
> 
>   - SSM may not understand local shopping habits → may need unfamiliar distribution channels → harder to enter retail markets
>   - May miss consumer trends (e.g. demand for eco-friendly products)
>   - May lack awareness of competitors’ brands and pricing → hard to compete if rivals are well-established
>   - Unfamiliarity with local legal controls → risk of non-compliance
> - **Import restrictions**
> 
>   - Tariffs could raise SSM’s prices → less competitive than domestic brands → reduced sales Quotas could limit export volume → restricted sales and potential price increases due to limited supply
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Cultural differences: Hardest to overcome as customer preferences may differ greatly from SSM’s offering Lack of knowledge: Significant but manageable through market research and adaptation Import restrictions: Most difficult to avoid due to government policies; may severely limit competitiveness and sales

**Extract:**

**Vegetable Palace (VP) **

VP was started 10 years ago in country Z. It is a public limited company. VP has a chain of 500 fast-food restaurants that operate across country Z. The VP brand is famous for its vegetarian food, this means none of its meals contain meat.

VP has a head office in Main City where all the directors and senior managers work. There are many barriers to communication. Each VP restaurant has a Manager, an Assistant Manager and 50 employees who cook and serve the meals. Restaurant Managers are often very busy and they are considering delegating some of their tasks to the Assistant Managers.

The ingredients for the restaurants are ordered in bulk by head office and then distributed from its warehouse to each of the restaurants. However, some senior managers think that Restaurant Managers should purchase their own ingredients from local suppliers. This would mean the ingredients would be fresher and would allow variations in the meals served.

VP wants to expand into another country. It will choose between the two countries shown in Appendix 2. VP will also need to decide how to enter a new market in another country. It has the option of forming a joint venture with another business or franchising the VP brand. The choice of finance will need to be considered for the expansion and the amount of finance will depend on the option chosen.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for VP's restaurants **

Choose VP for the finest vegetarian meals. Our service is the fastest possible!

You will receive your meal in less than 5 minutes – guaranteed!

Delicious and varied meals for even the biggest of appetites and all at competitive prices.

New meals are being introduced all the time.

There is a VP restaurant near you – we look forward to serving you soon.

**Appendix 2 **

**Summary of the two possible countries that VP could choose to locate its new restaurants.**

|   | **Country A** | **Country B** |
|---|---|---|
| **Raw materials** | Average variable cost \$6 per meal | Average variable cost \$2 per meal |
| **Labour** | Low unemployment \$10 per hour for each employee | High unemployment \$5 per hour for each employee |
| **Market** | Many competitors Average price per meal = \$20 | Few competitors Average price per meal = \$10 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Email from VP’s Managing Director to VP’s Marketing Director **

To: VP’s Marketing Director

From: VP’s Managing Director

Date: 31 March 2023

Re: Economic changes in country Z

Did you see the news this morning that interest rates will be raised from 3% to 5% later today? This will have several effects on our business in country Z.

The news also said that the exchange rate in country Z has depreciated. We will have to consider how this will affect our business, especially as we import 30% of our ingredients into country Z.

There are also new legal controls being introduced that mean we have to list all the ingredients used in each of our meals on the menu. We do reprint menus every time we change the meals, but it is something to consider.

Speak later today.

Consider the benefits and limitations of the following **two **ways VP can enter a new market in another country.

- Joint venture
- Franchising

Which way should VP choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf) when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
A joint venture would partner VP with a local business, which could provide valuable knowledge about customer preferences, regulations, and suppliers **[An]**. For example, VP might learn which vegetarian ingredients are popular or how to adapt its menu to local tastes **[Ap]**. The partner could also contribute capital, reducing VP's financial risks **[An]**

However, joint ventures can lead to conflicts over control and decision-making. VP might disagree with its partner about menu changes **[Ap]** or quality standards, potentially damaging its brand reputation **[An]**

Franchising would allow VP to expand rapidly while maintaining control over its brand. Franchisees are responsible for start-up costs and local management, reducing VP's financial investment and risk **[An]**. This could be particularly beneficial if VP chooses Country A, where average meal prices are lower **[Ap]**, potentially limiting profitability

However, franchising might make it difficult for VP to ensure consistent quality across all locations **[An]**, such as its commitment to serve meals in under 5 minutes **[Ap]**

VP should choose franchising to enter the new market **[E]**. This option aligns better with VP's existing business model of operating a large chain of restaurants **[Ap]**. Franchising would use VP's strong brand and efficient operating procedures **[Ap] **while benefiting from franchisees' local knowledge and investment **[E]**. It would enable fast expansion, helping VP establish a strong presence before competitors enter the market **[E]**. It would also mean that, unlike in a joint venture, it would not have to share its success with another business **[E]**

> - Add a final Evaluation (E):

> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Joint venture**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Share money and risk → VP needs to borrow less capital
>     - Local partner knows customers → menu can match local tastes → higher sales
>     - Partner’s knowledge → VP can skip much market research → save time and cost
>     - Partner explains local rules → fewer cultural mistakes → lower entry risk
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Finding a good partner takes time → expansion may be delayed
>     - Two management teams → possible disagreements → higher costs and slower decisions
>     - Profits are shared → VP’s return on investment is lower
>     - Partner might add less value → deal could feel unfair to VP
> - **Franchising**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Franchisee pays to open outlets → fast growth with little VP capital
>     - Up-front fee + royalties → extra income for VP
>     - No new loans or shares → VP avoids interest payments and share dilution
>   - **Disadvantages**

> - VP should choose the option that best balances local knowledge with control over quality and brand

parts.solutionMd:
Titanic Toys (TT) could benefit from purchasing economies that would allow TT to get discounts when buying large quantities of materials to make toys **[Ap]**. This could lower costs and increase profits **[An]**. Technical economies would let TT use more specialised machines in its factory. TT already has some specialist equipment for flow production **[Ap]**, so it could add even more advanced machines to speed up toy manufacturing. This would increase efficiency and lower production costs **[An]**. Financial economies mean TT could borrow money more cheaply to fund its expansion plans **[An]**, like building a new factory in country Z **[Ap]**

Technical economies are likely to have the greatest effect on TT's profit  **[E]**. TT is already using flow production and lean methods like Kaizen **[Ap]**, so new specialised machines would fit well with its existing processes. More advanced equipment would speed up production significantly, allowing TT to make more toys in less time. This would lower the cost per toy **[Ap]** and increase productivity. TT could then either lower prices to be more competitive in country Z or keep prices the same for higher profits **[An]**

While purchasing economies could reduce material costs, TT may already get some bulk discounts **[E]** as a large company **[Ap]**. Financial economies would help with expansion costs, but TT might use its own money rather than borrowing **[E]**. Therefore, technical economies offer the biggest opportunity to lower production costs and increase output, leading to higher profits as TT grows and enters new markets like country Z **[E]**

parts.problemMd: **Define **'joint venture'.
parts.solutionMd:
A joint venture occurs when two businesses agree to join together to share their knowledge, resources and skills** [K] **to form a separate business entity **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse joint ventures, which are usually temporary arrangements between businesses, with mergers or takeovers, which are the permanent integration of two of more businesses

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - A joint venture occurs when two businesses agree to join together to share their knowledge, resources and skills [K] to form a separate business entity [K]
> 
>   - OR, A joint venture is a partnership between two firms [K] where they create a new and distinct business together [K]
>   - OR, A temporary or permanent collaboration between businesses [K] to operate a shared enterprise as a new legal entity [K]
> - Partial definitions: When two businesses work together on a shared project [K]
> 
>   - OR, An agreement between two companies to combine resources [K]

parts.problemMd: Do you think a joint venture is the best way for a business to enter a new market in another country? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Joint ventures allow businesses to share expertise and resources **[K]**, which can help when entering unfamiliar markets. The local partner can provide knowledge about customer tastes and regulations in that country, reducing risk **[An]**

However, joint ventures can lead to disagreements over important decisions **[K]**, especially if objectives change over time. This could delay progress in the new market. Setting up a wholly-owned subsidiary might give the business more control, though it would be riskier **[An]**

Overall, if the owners are happy to share control, a joint venture is the best way, as it helps reduce the risks of setting up in a new country** [E]**. Expanding on their own may be too expensive or may not even be possible, as some governments insist that overseas businesses operate in partnership with local businesses** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Joint venture
> 
>   - Gains important local information about customers [k]; better able to meet customer requirements [an], helping to ensure sales [an]
>   - Wider range of contacts / better access to resources [k]; may obtain cheaper resources [an], reducing production costs [an].
>   - Less competition [k]; working with a local business reduces rivalry [an], helping increase market share [an]
>   - Access to specialist staff and technology [k]
>   - Clash of management styles [k]; may lead to conflict or decision-making issues [an]
>   - Must share profits [k]
> - Other options may include:
> 
>   - Franchising [k]; reduces the problem of lacking local knowledge [an], but may negatively affect brand reputation [an]
>   - Licensing [k]; may result in losing control over production quality [an]
>   - Expanding independently [k]; allows the business to retain all profits [an]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - A joint venture allows the business to gain important local information about customers [k], making it better able to meet their needs [an] and secure sales [an]
>   - Expanding independently would require more capital [k].
>   - If the business is willing to share control, a joint venture is the best option as it reduces the risks of entering a new market [eval]; especially since expanding alone may be too costly [eval]

parts.problemMd: Do you think a partnership is the best form of business organisation for a new business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
Partnerships allow entrepreneurs to share workload and responsibility **[K]**, so they can focus on different business activities. Partners bring more ideas and skills, making the business more competitive and  likely to succeed **[An]**

However, there's a risk of disagreements **[K] **between partners, which could slow decision-making and make it less responsive to customer needs **[An]**

For a new business, a partnership is often the best option if the partners have complementary skills and work well together **[E]**. However, the potential for conflict means it's not always the best choice. The best form of organisation depends on the specific situation of the new business **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Partnership
>   
>     - Share workload/responsibility [k]; allows each partner to focus on different areas of the business [an]
>     - More ideas/skills [k]; can help make the business more competitive [an]
>     - Can share potential losses and risks [k]
>     - Unlimited liability [k]; personal possessions at risk if business debts cannot be paid [an]
>     - Risk of disagreements / slower decision-making [k]; which could make the business less responsive to customer demand [an].
>     - Must share any profits made [k]
> - Other options might include:
> 
>   - Sole Trader [k]
>   
>     - Simple to set up with very little paperwork [an]
>     - Requires limited start-up capital [an] Makes all decisions and has full control of the business [an]
>     - Keeps all the profit [an]
>     - Has limited access to finance [an]
>   - Private Limited Company (Ltd) [k]
>   
>     - Benefits from limited liability
>     - More paperwork and legal requirements to set up and operate [an]
>   - Justification might include:
>   
>     - A partnership allows owners to share the workload [k], giving each partner time to specialise in specific areas of the business [an]
>     - However, the major drawback is unlimited liability [k], meaning personal possessions are at risk if the business cannot repay debts [an]
>     - Despite this, a partnership may be a better option than a sole trader — while both have unlimited liability, a partnership allows risk-sharing and brings extra skills [eval], which could reduce potential problems and increase the chances of success [eval]

**Extract:**

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business.

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

**Explain one **advantage and **one **disadvantage to Tokumbo of being a sole trader.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
Tokumbo has complete control over SA **[K]** and can make all the decisions without having to consult anyone else **[An]**. For example, Tokumbo can decide whether to start offering new types of safari tours, like the camping option for young people or the luxury tours for high-income tourists **[Ap]**. He can quickly respond to changes, such as the new trends in the market **[An]**

However, as a sole trader, Tokumbo has unlimited liability **[K]**. If SA gets into financial trouble, Tokumbo is personally responsible for all the debts **[An]** and might have to sell personal possessions to cover costs. This is a risk, especially since SA has only been operating for 2 years **[Ap]** and the business environment is changing with increased competition and rising inflation in country X **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two full paragraphs, one for each reason/point
> - In each paragraph:
> 
>   - State one valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain how it works using a cause–effect chain → up to 2 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant advantages might include:
> 
>   - Complete control / decision-making power – the owner makes all business decisions independently; enjoys being his own boss with no one to report to; for example, can decide whether to start offering new safari tours
>   - Keeps all the profit – as the sole owner, he retains all profits from the business without sharing returns from his hard work, even while employing 5 staff
>   - Easy to set up – few legal requirements make the start-up process simpler and cheaper, with lower setup costs like accountancy fees
>   - Freedom over working hours and holidays – unlike when employed at a holiday company with fixed hours, he can now choose his schedule, allowing flexibility during quiet periods
>   - Complete privacy – does not have to publish financial details publicly; only required to share information with the tax office
> - Relevant disadvantages might include:
> 
>   - Unlimited liability – the owner's personal possessions are at risk if the business fails, not just the money invested in the business
>   - No one to share responsibility or decisions with – all decisions rest with the owner, which can be stressful and may lead to mistakes
>   - No continuity – if the owner dies, the business ends, unlike a limited company that has a separate legal identity and can continue through share ownership
>   - Lack of capital / difficulty raising finance – relies solely on the owner's funds or borrowing, which may restrict future expansion
>   - Heavy workload / long hours – managing all aspects of the business can be time-consuming, making holidays and breaks more difficult
> - Possible application points include:
> 
>   - Safari holidays
>   - Increase in tourists from other countries
>   - High-income / luxury safari tourists
>   - Business operating for 2 years
>   - Game reserve setting
>   - Camping / tent accommodation
>   - Wild animals
>   - 4 safari guides, 4 safari vehicles
>   - Local or luxury hotel accommodation
>   - Fuel use

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> LMA is a family-owned restaurant. The business was started 20 years ago and has remained small. LMA is a partnership. The partners are considering whether LMA should become a private limited company. The Finance Manager is analysing LMA’s cash-flow forecast. An extract is shown below.
> 
> | **Extract from LMA’s cash-flow forecast 2023 (\$000)** |   |   |   |
> |---|---|---|---|
> |   | **July** | **August** | **September** |
> | Cash inflow | 420 | 300 | 330 |
> | Cash outflow | 410 | 320 | 360 |
> | Net cash flow | **X** | (20) | (30) |
> | Opening balance | 60 | 70 | 50 |
> | Closing balance | 70 | 50 | **Y** |

**Explain one **advantage and **one **disadvantage to LMA of  becoming a private limited company.
parts.solutionMd:
One advantage of becoming a private limited company is limited liability for LMA's owners **[K]**. As a partnership, the owners have unlimited liability so are personally responsible for all of LMA's debts. By changing to a private limited company, the owners' liability would be limited to the amount invested in the restaurant. This protects their personal assets, such as homes **[An]**, if LMA were to fail after 20 years of operation **[Ap]**

However, there are more legal formalities **[K]**. As a private limited company, LMA would need to publish its accounts and hold annual general meetings. This takes time away from running the family-owned restaurant **[Ap]** and reduces privacy for owners. After remaining small for two decades as a partnership, adapting to these new requirements could be challenging and time-consuming for LMA **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Advantages:
>   
>     - Limited liability [k]; personal assets are not at risk if the business cannot repay its debts — owners are only liable for the amount invested [an]
>     - Separate legal identity [k]; owners are not personally responsible for business actions [an], unlike in a partnership [app]
>     - Able to raise finance by selling shares [k]; to fund expansion [an] if the business chooses not to remain small [app]
>     - Continuity [k] – the business continues even if ownership changes
>     - Can choose who buys shares [k] – allows control over who becomes involved in the business
>   - Disadvantages:
>   
>     - More legal formalities [k]; which take time away from running other activities [an], such as the restaurant [app]
>     - Separation of ownership and control [k]; owners may not be involved in or agree with business decisions [an], especially if directors don’t listen to the family [app]
>     - Expensive and time-consuming to change to this business structure [k]
>     - Accounts must be made publicly available [k] – reducing financial privacy
>     - Dividends may need to be paid to shareholders [k]; reducing the amount of retained profit available to reinvest [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

**Extract:**

**Protective Hats (PH)**

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for PH’s products**

PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work.

We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

High quality is guaranteed.

PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

**Appendix 2**

**Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director

From: Human Resources Director

Date: 1 October 2023

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

**Appendix 3 **

**PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

**Explain two **advantages and **two** disadvantages of PH being a public limited company.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solutionMd:
PH can sell shares to the public **[K]** to finance the plans to open factories in other countries** [Ap]**.

Secondly, PH's owners benefit from limited liability **[K]**, protecting shareholders' personal assets if the business expansion fails **[Ap]**

However, PH must publish its accounts **[K]**, allowing PH's competitors **[Ap] **to view this information to gain a competitive advantage and gain market share

As a public limited company, PH may be at risk of takeover **[K]**. The current owners could lose control of the company they've successfully run for 50 years **[Ap]**

> 
> - Relevant answers might include
> 
>   - Advantages:
>   
>     - Can sell shares to the public – attractive to potential shareholders, especially as the business has a long history of producing high-quality products
>     - Limited liability – protects shareholders' personal assets, which is important when expanding into other countries
>     - Continuity – if shareholders die, their shares are passed on; this has helped the company operate successfully for over 50 years.

>     - Protective hats

Knowledge of new technology is crucial because the spa is still using old equipment while competitors have upgraded **[Ap]**. A partner with technology knowledge could help modernise the spa's equipment and systems, such as implementing software to ease customer bookings and accounting, which Bethany currently does manually **[Ap]**, taking her a long time when she could be focusing on improving other aspects of the business  **[An]**

Experience in managing a health spa is important as it would complement Bethany's skills. Bethany currently does all the administration herself **[Ap]** when the spa is closed. An experienced partner could take on some management responsibilities, giving Bethany more of the free time as she desires **[An]**. Their industry experience could also help BB Health Spa compete against nearby spas that charge much higher prices **[Ap]**

Capital to invest is vital because new technology and equipment for health spas are very expensive **[Ap]**. BB Health Spa likely needs significant funds to upgrade its outdated equipment and implement new booking and accounting systems **[Ap]**. A partner bringing capital could allow these improvements without Bethany having to take on debt **[An]**

While all three factors are important, and the ideal partner would possess all of these characteristics,  knowledge of new technology is likely the most crucial **[E] **for BB Health Spa's future success in the changing industry **[Ap]**. It is already lagging behind competitors **[Ap]** in this respect and, if it is going to remain competitive, the business must become more efficient. Technology is a key way to do this **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Knowledge of new technology**
> 
>   - Operates the latest treatment machines → less staff training → lower costs
>   - Can train other employees → new treatments introduced faster → spa gains an edge over rivals
>   - Possible drawback: partner might feel “more important” than Bethany → tension over who is in charge
> - **Experience in managing a health spa**
> 
>   - Knows day-to-day operations → runs the spa more efficiently → wastes less time and money
>   - Can take over tasks like ordering stock → frees Bethany’s time, which is her main reason for a partnership
>   - Risk of clashes if the partner’s style differs → arguments could hurt efficiency
> - **Capital to invest**
> 
>   - Brings cash for the latest equipment → no bank loan needed → saves interest costs
>   - Extra funds make it easier to expand and match bigger spas with modern treatments
>   - Drawback: partner will want a share of profit and a voice in decisions, reducing Bethany’s control
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Experience in managing a spa would give Bethany the free time she wants, but she might still need to borrow money for new equipment
>   - Knowledge of new technology boosts competitiveness and speeds up training, yet it does not add capital and could leave Bethany doing most management tasks herself
>   - Capital investment removes loan costs and funds expansion, but it will not lighten Bethany’s workload and means sharing control and profits
